1: #' Confidence interval for a Pearson correlation, adjusted for AR(1) autocorrelation
2: #'
3: #' Computes a confidence interval (and optional zero-correlation test) for the
4: #' Pearson correlation between two serially correlated series. It reduces the
5: #' nominal sample size N to an effective sample size N_eff based on each series'
6: #' lag-1 autocorrelation, then applies Fisher's z-transformation using N_eff.
7: #'
8: #' @param x,y       Numeric vectors of equal length (paired observations).
9: #' @param conf      Confidence level (default 0.95).
10: #'
11: #' @return A list with the correlation, effective sample size, CI bounds,
12: #'         and a t-test of H0: rho = 0 using N_eff.
13: #' @export
14: corr_ci_autocorr <- function(x, y, conf = 0.95) {
15: 
16:   # --- input handling: drop pairs with NA, check length ---------------------
17:   ok <- stats::complete.cases(x, y)
18:   x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]
19:   n <- length(x)
20:   if (n < 4L) stop("Need at least 4 complete paired observations.")
21: 
22:   # --- Pearson correlation --------------------------------------------------
23:   r <- stats::cor(x, y)
24: 
25:   # --- lag-1 autocorrelation of each series ---------------------------------
26:   rho_x <- stats::acf(x, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE, demean = TRUE)$acf[2]
27:   rho_y <- stats::acf(y, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE, demean = TRUE)$acf[2]
28: 
29:   # --- effective sample size for two AR(1) processes ------------------------
30:   #   N_eff = N * (1 - rho_x * rho_y) / (1 + rho_x * rho_y)
31:   prod_rho <- rho_x * rho_y
32:   n_eff <- n * (1 - prod_rho) / (1 + prod_rho)
33:   # Guard against pathological values; N_eff must exceed 3 for the SE below.
34:   n_eff <- min(n_eff, n)            # cap at nominal N (negative prod_rho case)
35:   if (n_eff <= 3) {
36:     warning("Effective sample size <= 3; interval is unreliable.")
37:     return(list(
38:       r          = r,
39:       conf       = conf,
40:       ci_lower   = NA_real_,
41:       ci_upper   = NA_real_,
42:       n          = n,
43:       n_eff      = n_eff,
44:       rho_x      = rho_x,
45:       rho_y      = rho_y,
46:       t_stat     = NA_real_,
47:       df         = n_eff - 2,
48:       p_value    = NA_real_
49:     ))
50:   }
51: 
52:   # --- Fisher z-transform and CI -------------------------------------------
53:   z      <- atanh(r)
54:   se_z   <- 1 / sqrt(n_eff - 3)
55:   zcrit  <- stats::qnorm(1 - (1 - conf) / 2)
56:   ci     <- tanh(z + c(-1, 1) * zcrit * se_z)   # back-transform to r-space
57: 
58:   # --- significance test of H0: rho = 0, using N_eff ------------------------
59:   t_stat <- r * sqrt((n_eff - 2) / (1 - r^2))
60:   df     <- n_eff - 2
61:   p_val  <- 2 * stats::pt(-abs(t_stat), df = df)
62: 
63:   list(
64:     r          = r,
65:     conf       = conf,
66:     ci_lower   = ci[1],
67:     ci_upper   = ci[2],
68:     n          = n,
69:     n_eff      = n_eff,
70:     rho_x      = rho_x,
71:     rho_y      = rho_y,
72:     t_stat     = t_stat,
73:     df         = df,
74:     p_value    = p_val
75:   )
76: }
77: 
78: #' Little simulation, testing if no-multicollinearity == unbiased estimates
79: #'
80: #' Simulates `n` observations where `y = a*x1 + b*x2 + e`, with `x1` and `x2`
81: #' drawn independently (so no multicollinearity), then returns the estimated
82: #' coefficient of `x1` from a regression of `y` on `x1` alone.
83: #'
84: #' @param n Number of observations to simulate.
85: #' @param a True coefficient of `x1`.
86: #' @param b True coefficient of `x2`.
87: #'
88: #' @return The estimated coefficient of `x1` from `lm(y ~ x1)`.
89: #' @export
90: #'
91: #' @examples
92: #' hist(replicate(1000, lm_sim(100, -10, 10)))
93: lm_sim <- function(n, a, b) {
94: 
95:   x1 <- sample(1:100, size = n, replace = TRUE)
96:   x2 <- sample(1:100, size = n, replace = TRUE)
97: 
98:   e <- stats::rnorm(n)
99: 
100:   y <- a * x1 + b * x2 + e
101: 
102:   stats::coefficients(stats::lm(y ~ x1))[2]
103: }
104: 
105: 
106: #' Simulation to test how multi-collinearity affects estimates
107: #'
108: #' Simulates bivariate normal predictors `X1` and `X2` with covariance matrix
109: #' `covmat`, generates `Y = b0 + b1*X1 + b2*X2 + epsilon`, then fits three
110: #' regressions: the joint model (`Y ~ X2 + X1`) and each single-predictor
111: #' model. Returns the coefficient estimates from all three models stacked
112: #' together.
113: #'
114: #' @param n Number of observations to simulate.
115: #' @param mu1 Mean of `X1`.
116: #' @param mu2 Mean of `X2`.
117: #' @param b0 Intercept of the true model.
118: #' @param b1 True coefficient of `X1`.
119: #' @param b2 True coefficient of `X2`.
120: #' @param covmat 2x2 covariance matrix of `X1` and `X2`.
121: #'
122: #' @return A data frame with columns `term`, `value`, and `type` (`"joint"`
123: #'   for the joint model, `"single"` for the single-predictor models).
124: #' @export
125: #'
126: #' @examples
127: #' multicol_sim(
128: #'   n = 100, mu1 = 0, mu2 = 0, b0 = 1, b1 = 2, b2 = 3,
129: #'   covmat = matrix(c(1, 0.9, 0.9, 1), nrow = 2)
130: #' )
131: multicol_sim <- function(n, mu1, mu2, b0, b1, b2, covmat) {
132: 
133:   # Generate n random samples from a bivariate normal with covariance covmat
134:   L <- chol(covmat)
135:   z <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n * 2), nrow = n, ncol = 2)
136:   bivariate_data <- sweep(z %*% L, 2, c(mu1, mu2), "+")
137: 
138:   # Convert to a data frame for easier use
139:   df <- as.data.frame(bivariate_data)
140:   colnames(df) <- c("X1", "X2")
141: 
142:   # make linear model
143:   epsilon <- stats::rnorm(n)
144:   df$Y <- b0 + b1 * df$X1 + b2 * df$X2 + epsilon
145: 
146:   # estimate parameters
147:   modf <- data.frame(
148:     term = names(stats::coefficients(stats::lm(Y ~ X2 + X1, data = df))),
149:     value = unname(stats::coefficients(stats::lm(Y ~ X2 + X1, data = df)))
150:   )
151:   modf$type <- "joint"
152: 
153:   mod1 <- data.frame(
154:     term = names(stats::coefficients(stats::lm(Y ~ X1, data = df))),
155:     value = unname(stats::coefficients(stats::lm(Y ~ X1, data = df)))
156:   )
157:   mod1$type <- "single"
158: 
159:   mod2 <- data.frame(
160:     term = names(stats::coefficients(stats::lm(Y ~ X2, data = df))),
161:     value = unname(stats::coefficients(stats::lm(Y ~ X2, data = df)))
162:   )
163:   mod2$type <- "single"
164: 
165:   all_mod <- rbind(modf, mod1, mod2)
166: 
167:   return(all_mod)
168: }

1: #' Allele frequency after one generation of selection
2: #'
3: #' Computes the frequency of allele A after one generation of selection at a
4: #' single biallelic locus, assuming random mating and a fitness of
5: #' `1 + h*s` for heterozygotes and `1 + s` for AA homozygotes.
6: #'
7: #' @param q Current frequency of allele A.
8: #' @param h Dominance coefficient of allele A.
9: #' @param s Selection coefficient of allele A.
10: #'
11: #' @return The allele frequency of A in the next generation.
12: #' @export
13: #'
14: #' @examples
15: #' fitfreq(q = 0.1, h = 0.5, s = 0.01)
16: fitfreq <- function(q, h, s) {
17:   p <- 1 - q
18:   wbar <- (1) * p^2 + (1 + h * s) * 2 * p * q + (1 + s) * q^2
19:   (q^2 * (1 + s) + p * q * (1 + h * s)) / wbar
20: }
21: 
22: #' Allele frequency trajectory over time: apply selection, then drift comes from rbinom
23: #'
24: #' Simulates a Wright-Fisher trajectory of a biallelic locus under selection
25: #' and genetic drift. Each generation, the deterministic allele frequency
26: #' after selection is computed with [fitfreq()], then the number of A alleles
27: #' in the next generation is drawn from a binomial distribution.
28: #'
29: #' @param N Population size (number of diploid individuals).
30: #' @param q Initial frequency of allele A.
31: #' @param h Dominance coefficient of allele A.
32: #' @param s Selection coefficient of allele A. Either a scalar (recycled for
33: #'   every generation) or a vector of length `G - 1` giving the selection
34: #'   coefficient applied in each generation.
35: #' @param G Number of generations to simulate.
36: #'
37: #' @return A numeric vector of length `G` with the frequency of allele A in
38: #'   each generation.
39: #' @export
40: #'
41: #' @examples
42: #' WF.sel(N = 100, q = 0.1, h = 0.5, s = 0.01, G = 50)
43: WF.sel <- function(N, q, h, s, G) {
44:   if (length(s) == 1) {
45:     s <- rep(s, G - 1)
46:   } else if (length(s) != G - 1) {
47:     stop("s must be a scalar or a vector of length G - 1.")
48:   }
49: 
50:   counts <- numeric(G)
51:   counts[1] <- N * q
52:   for (i in 2:G) {
53:     counts[i] <- stats::rbinom(1, N, fitfreq(counts[i - 1] / N, h, s[i - 1]))
54:   }
55:   counts / N
56: }

Implementation sketch:
```r
multicol_sim <- function(n, mu1, mu2, b0, b1, b2, covmat) {
  L <- chol(covmat)
  z <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n * 2), nrow = n, ncol = 2)
  df <- as.data.frame(sweep(z %*% L, 2, c(mu1, mu2), "+"))
  colnames(df) <- c("X1", "X2")
  df$Y <- b0 + b1 * df$X1 + b2 * df$X2 + stats::rnorm(n)

  specs <- list(
    stats::as.formula("Y ~ X2 + X1", ...), # careful ordering
  )
}
```

```r
  form_list <- list(quote(Y ~ X2 + X1), quote(Y ~ X1), quote(Y ~ X2))
  types <- c("joint", "single", "single")
  fits <- lapply(form_list, function(f) f)
  out_list <- Map(function(f, tp) {
    coef <- stats::coefficients(stats::lm(f, data = df))
    data.frame(term = names(coef), value = unname(coef), type = tp)
  }, fits, types)
  do.call(rbind, out_list)
```

   - However, `statistics.R` and `popgen.R` use `stats::` everywhere — good.

   ```r
   coefs <- function(formula, data) {
     cf <- stats::coefficients(stats::lm(formula, data = data))
     data.frame(term = names(cf), value = unname(cf), type = type)
   }
   ```
   Behavior identical. This reduces repetition 3x and halves the lm() calls (efficiency win: 6 lm fits → 3).

3. **`save_plot` symlink removal** (plotting.R:38-44): the two if/file.remove blocks could be a small loop or just `unlink(c(symlink_pdf, symlink_png))` — `unlink()` on a non-existent path is a no-op with no warning. But careful: unlink returns 0/1 invisibly, and file.remove was used before. `unlink()` is arguably cleaner and doesn't warn. That's a safe simplification. Behavior identical.

Modern R best practice (tidyverse style, the style guide from Hadley) says avoid dots in function names, prefer snake_case. But renaming a public exported function changes the API. The user said "Only make changes that do not alter the functionality of the code" — renaming does not alter functionality per se but breaks user code that calls WF.sel. Actually the doc says "Current frequency of allele A" and h is dominance of allele A, fitness 1+h*s for heterozygotes and 1+s for AA. The formula uses q as the selected allele frequency. That's internally consistent though unconventional (usually p is the favored). Changing parameter names = API change. Leave, maybe not even mention. Or mention as optional.

  "newString": "multicol_sim <- function(n, mu1, mu2, b0, b1, b2, covmat) {\n\n  # Generate n random samples from a bivariate normal with covariance covmat\n  L <- chol(covmat)\n  z <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n * 2), nrow = n, ncol = 2)\n  bivariate_data <- sweep(z %*% L, 2, c(mu1, mu2), \"+\")\n\n  # Convert to a data frame for easier use\n  df <- as.data.frame(bivariate_data)\n  colnames(df) <- c(\"X1\", \"X2\")\n\n  # make linear model\n  epsilon <- stats::rnorm(n)\n  df$Y <- b0 + b1 * df$X1 + b2 * df$X2 + epsilon\n\n  # Stack coefficient estimates from the joint model and each single-predictor\n  # model into one data frame\n  coef_table <- function(formula, type) {\n    coefs <- stats::coefficients(stats::lm(formula, data = df))\n    data.frame(term = names(coefs), value = unname(coefs), type = type)\n  }\n\n  rbind(\n    coef_table(Y ~ X2 + X1, \"joint\"),\n    coef_table(Y ~ X1, \"single\"),\n    coef_table(Y ~ X2, \"single\")\n  )\n}",
  "oldString": "multicol_sim <- function(n, mu1, mu2, b0, b1, b2, covmat) {\n\n  # Generate n random samples from a bivariate normal with covariance covmat\n  L <- chol(covmat)\n  z <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n * 2), nrow = n, ncol = 2)\n  bivariate_data <- sweep(z %*% L, 2, c(mu1, mu2), \"+\")\n\n  # Convert to a data frame for easier use\n  df <- as.data.frame(bivariate_data)\n  colnames(df) <- c(\"X1\", \"X2\")\n\n  # make linear model\n  epsilon <- stats::rnorm(n)\n  df$Y <- b0 + b1 * df$X1 + b2 * df$X2 + epsilon\n\n  # estimate parameters\n  modf <- data.frame(\n    term = names(stats::coefficients(stats::lm(Y ~ X2 + X1, data = df))),\n    value = unname(stats::coefficients(stats::lm(Y ~ X2 + X1, data = df)))\n  )\n  modf$type <- \"joint\"\n\n  mod1 <- data.frame(\n    term = names(stats::coefficients(stats::lm(Y ~ X1, data = df))),\n    value = unname(stats::coefficients(stats::lm(Y ~ X1, data = df)))\n  )\n  mod1$type <- \"single\"\n\n  mod2 <- data.frame(\n    term = names(stats::coefficients(stats::lm(Y ~ X2, data = df))),\n    value = unname(stats::coefficients(stats::lm(Y ~ X2, data = df)))\n  )\n  mod2$type <- \"single\"\n\n  all_mod <- rbind(modf, mod1, mod2)\n\n  return(all_mod)\n}"
}

## User
Add this function to plotting: # compare predicted values to true values for a continuous variable as a scatterplot
compare_predictions_truth_scatter = function(predictions, truth, model_labels, truthlab, predlab, colorvar, colorlab){
  
  # replace non-numbers with NA so that correlation still works
  print("Omit non-numbers")
  print(length(predictions))
  print(length(truth))
  print(length(colorvar))
  
  filter = !(is.nan(predictions) | is.nan(truth) | is.infinite(predictions) | is.infinite(truth))
  
  predictions = predictions[filter]
  truth = truth[filter] 
  colorvar = colorvar[filter]
  
  print(length(predictions))
  print(length(truth))
  print(length(colorvar))
   
  # Calculate correlation between truth and results
  # spearman correlation is invariant to log transforms
  my_cor_coeff = cor.test(predictions, truth, method = "pearson")
  print(my_cor_coeff)
  cor_est = signif(my_cor_coeff$estimate, digits = 3)
  cor_lwb = signif(my_cor_coeff$conf.int[1], digits = 3)
  cor_upb = signif(my_cor_coeff$conf.int[2], digits = 3)
  #cor_pvalue = signif(my_cor_coeff$p.value, digits = 2)
  cor_n = length(truth)
  
  # root mean square error
  rmse <- signif(sqrt(mean((predictions - truth)^2)), digits = 3)
  
  # plot data
  plotdata = data.frame(predictions = predictions, truth = truth, colorvar = colorvar)
  
  p = ggplot(aes(y = predictions, x = truth, color = colorvar), data = plotdata) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "#8C0172", linewidth = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#9B951B", linewidth = 2) +
  scale_color_continuous(low = "#04050A", high = "#F9CCF9") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 16)) +
  labs(x = truthlab, 
       y = predlab,
       title = paste(model_labels, "\nr = ", cor_est, ", n = " , cor_n, "\n95 % CI = [",  cor_lwb, ", ", cor_upb, "]\nRMSE = ", rmse, sep = ""),
       color = colorlab)
  
  return(p)
}

  "newString": "  for (sub_data in data_list) {\n    print(plot_fn(sub_data))\n  }\n\n  invisible(filepath)\n}\n\n#' Scatterplot comparing predictions to true values\n#'\n#' Plots predicted values against true values for a continuous variable, with\n#' the identity line (predictions = truth), a linear fit, and the Pearson\n#' correlation with 95% CI, sample size, and RMSE in the plot title. Pairs\n#' where either variable is NA, NaN, or infinite are dropped before analysis.\n#'\n#' @param predictions Numeric vector of predicted values.\n#' @param truth Numeric vector of true values, same length as `predictions`.\n#' @param model_label Model name shown in the plot title.\n#' @param truth_label Axis label for the true values.\n#' @param pred_label Axis label for the predicted values.\n#' @param color_var Numeric vector mapped to point color, same length as\n#'   `predictions`.\n#' @param color_label Legend title for the color scale.\n#'\n#' @return A ggplot object.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' set.seed(1)\n#' truth <- rnorm(100)\n#' compare_predictions_truth_scatter(\n#'   predictions = truth + rnorm(100, sd = 0.5),\n#'   truth = truth,\n#'   model_label = \"Example model\",\n#'   truth_label = \"Truth\",\n#'   pred_label = \"Prediction\",\n#'   color_var = truth,\n#'   color_label = \"True value\"\n#' )\ncompare_predictions_truth_scatter <- function(predictions, truth, model_label,\n                                              truth_label, pred_label,\n                                              color_var, color_label) {\n  keep <- !(is.na(predictions) | is.nan(predictions) | is.infinite(predictions) |\n    is.na(truth) | is.nan(truth) | is.infinite(truth))\n  predictions <- predictions[keep]\n  truth <- truth[keep]\n  color_var <- color_var[keep]\n\n  # Pearson correlation is invariant to log transforms of either variable\n  cor_test <- stats::cor.test(predictions, truth, method = \"pearson\")\n  cor_est <- signif(cor_test$estimate, digits = 3)\n  cor_lwb <- signif(cor_test$conf.int[1], digits = 3)\n  cor_upb <- signif(cor_test$conf.int[2], digits = 3)\n  cor_n <- length(truth)\n\n  rmse <- signif(sqrt(mean((predictions - truth)^2)), digits = 3)\n\n  plotdata <- data.frame(predictions = predictions, truth = truth, color_var = color_var)\n\n  ggplot2::ggplot(aes(y = predictions, x = truth, color = color_var), data = plotdata) +\n    ggplot2::geom_point() +\n    ggplot2::geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = \"#8C0172\", linewidth = 2) +\n    ggplot2::geom_smooth(method = \"lm\", color = \"#9B951B\", linewidth = 2) +\n    ggplot2::scale_color_continuous(low = \"#04050A\", high = \"#F9CCF9\") +\n    ggplot2::theme_classic() +\n    ggplot2::theme(text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 16)) +\n    ggplot2::labs(\n      x = truth_label,\n      y = pred_label,\n      title = paste(\n        model_label, \"\\nr = \", cor_est, \", n = \", cor_n,\n        \"\\n95 % CI = [\", cor_lwb, \", \", cor_upb, \"]\",\n        \"\\nRMSE = \", rmse,\n        sep = \"\"\n      ),\n      color = color_label\n    )\n}",
  "oldString": "  for (sub_data in data_list) {\n    print(plot_fn(sub_data))\n  }\n\n  invisible(filepath)\n}"
}

  filter(alen >= 1000, mapq >= 1)

# ---- 3. Orient reverse-strand alignments for correct diagonal direction ----

PAF files written by `minimap2 --paf` have\n#'   no header row; extra columns beyond the 12 mandatory ones are ignored.\n#'\n#' @return A tibble with 13 columns: the 12 mandatory PAF fields\n#'   (`qname`, `qlen`, `qstart`, `qend`, `strand`, `tname`, `tlen`,\n#'   `tstart`, `tend`, `nmatch`, `alen`, `mapq` \u2014 all but `qname`, `strand`,\n#'   and `tname` numeric) plus `pident` (`nmatch / alen`).\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' \\dontrun{\n#' paf <- read_paf(\"hap2_vs_hap1.paf\")\n#' }\nread_paf <- function(file) {\n  paf_cols <- c(\n    \"qname\", \"qlen\", \"qstart\", \"qend\", \"strand\",\n    \"tname\", \"tlen\", \"tstart\", \"tend\",\n    \"nmatch\", \"alen\", \"mapq\"\n  )\n\n  paf <- readr::read_tsv(\n    file,\n    col_names = FALSE,\n    col_types = readr::cols(.default = \"c\"),\n    show_col_types = FALSE\n  )\n  paf <- paf[, seq_len(12)]\n  names(paf) <- paf_cols\n\n  paf <- dplyr::mutate(\n    paf,\n    dplyr::across(\n      c(qlen, qstart, qend, tlen, tstart, tend, nmatch, alen, mapq),\n      as.numeric\n    ),\n    pident = nmatch / alen\n  )\n\n  paf\n}",

{

  "newString": "    ggplot2::labs(\n      x = truth_label,\n      y = pred_label,\n      title = paste(\n        model_label, \"\\nr = \", cor_est, \", n = \", cor_n,\n        \"\\n95 % CI = [\", cor_lwb, \", \", cor_upb, \"]\",\n        \"\\nRMSE = \", rmse,\n        sep = \"\"\n      ),\n      color = color_label\n    )\n}\n\n#' Dotplot of PAF alignments between two sequences\n#'\n#' Plots alignment blocks from a PAF data frame (as returned by [read_paf()])\n#' as line segments: query coordinates on the x axis, target coordinates on\n#' the y axis, colored by strand. Reverse-strand blocks are oriented so that\n#' collinear alignments lie on a shared diagonal. Low-quality blocks can be\n#' dropped via `min_alen`/`min_mapq`.\n#'\n#' @param paf A PAF data frame from [read_paf()].\n#' @param q_seq Query sequence name to plot (`qname`).\n#' @param t_seq Target sequence name to plot (`tname`).\n#' @param xlab X-axis label (query).\n#' @param ylab Y-axis label (target).\n#' @param title Plot title.\n#' @param min_alen Minimum alignment block length to plot (default 1000).\n#' @param min_mapq Minimum mapping quality to plot (default 1).\n#'\n#' @return A ggplot object. Add highlights (e.g. [ggplot2::geom_hline()]) and\n#'   save it with [save_plot()].\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' paf <- data.frame(\n#'   qname = c(\"q1\", \"q1\", \"q1\", \"q2\"),\n#'   qlen = 1000, qstart = c(100, 500, 100, 100), qend = c(400, 900, 400, 400),\n#'   strand = c(\"+\", \"+\", \"-\", \"+\"),\n#'   tname = c(\"t1\", \"t1\", \"t1\", \"t2\"),\n#'   tlen = 1000, tstart = c(200, 600, 700, 200),\n#'   tend = c(500, 1000, 1000, 500),\n#'   nmatch = c(290, 390, 380, 290),\n#'   alen = c(300, 400, 400, 300),\n#'   mapq = c(60, 60, 60, 0)\n#' )\n#' p <- plot_paf_dotplot(paf, q_seq = \"q1\", t_seq = \"t1\",\n#'                       xlab = \"Query q1\", ylab = \"Target t1\",\n#'                       title = \"Demo dotplot\")\nplot_paf_dotplot <- function(paf, q_seq, t_seq, xlab, ylab, title,\n                             min_alen = 1000, min_mapq = 1) {\n  paf_f <- dplyr::filter(paf, alen >= min_alen, mapq >= min_mapq)\n\n  # Orient reverse-strand alignments for correct diagonal direction\n  paf_plot <- dplyr::mutate(\n    paf_f,\n    tstart_plot = dplyr::if_else(strand == \"-\", tend, tstart),\n    tend_plot = dplyr::if_else(strand == \"-\", tstart, tend)\n  )\n\n  paf_plot <- dplyr::filter(paf_plot, qname == q_seq, tname == t_seq)\n  if (nrow(paf_plot) == 0) {\n    stop(\"No alignments found between '\", q_seq, \"' and '\", t_seq, \"'.\")\n  }\n\n  ggplot2::ggplot(paf_plot) +\n    ggplot2::geom_segment(\n      ggplot2::aes(\n        x = qstart, xend = qend,\n        y = tstart_plot, yend = tend_plot,\n        color = strand\n      ),\n      linewidth = 0.6\n    ) +\n    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(\n      values = c(\"+\" = \"steelblue\", \"-\" = \"firebrick\")\n    ) +\n    ggplot2::labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, title = title, color = \"Strand\") +\n    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +\n    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())\n}",

155: }
156: 
157: #' Dotplot of PAF alignments between two sequences
158: #'
159: #' Plots alignment blocks from a PAF data frame (as returned by [read_paf()])
160: #' as line segments: query coordinates on the x axis, target coordinates on
161: #' the y axis, colored by strand. Reverse-strand blocks are oriented so that
162: #' collinear alignments lie on a shared diagonal. Low-quality blocks can be
163: #' dropped via `min_alen`/`min_mapq`.
164: #'
165: #' @param paf A PAF data frame from [read_paf()].
166: #' @param q_seq Query sequence name to plot (`qname`).
167: #' @param t_seq Target sequence name to plot (`tname`).
168: #' @param xlab X-axis label (query).
169: #' @param ylab Y-axis label (target).
170: #' @param title Plot title.
171: #' @param min_alen Minimum alignment block length to plot (default 1000).
172: #' @param min_mapq Minimum mapping quality to plot (default 1).
173: #'
174: #' @return A ggplot object. Add highlights (e.g. [ggplot2::geom_hline()]) and
175: #'   save it with [save_plot()].
176: #' @export
177: #'
178: #' @examples
179: #' paf <- data.frame(
180: #'   qname = c("q1", "q1", "q1", "q2"),
181: #'   qlen = 1000, qstart = c(100, 500, 100, 100), qend = c(400, 900, 400, 400),
182: #'   strand = c("+", "+", "-", "+"),
183: #'   tname = c("t1", "t1", "t1", "t2"),
184: #'   tlen = 1000, tstart = c(200, 600, 700, 200),
185: #'   tend = c(500, 1000, 1000, 500),
186: #'   nmatch = c(290, 390, 380, 290),
187: #'   alen = c(300, 400, 400, 300),
188: #'   mapq = c(60, 60, 60, 0)
189: #' )
190: #' p <- plot_paf_dotplot(paf, q_seq = "q1", t_seq = "t1",
191: #'                       xlab = "Query q1", ylab = "Target t1",
192: #'                       title = "Demo dotplot")
193: plot_paf_dotplot <- function(paf, q_seq, t_seq, xlab, ylab, title,
194:                              min_alen = 1000, min_mapq = 1) {
195:   paf_f <- dplyr::filter(paf, alen >= min_alen, mapq >= min_mapq)
196: 
197:   # Orient reverse-strand alignments for correct diagonal direction
198:   paf_plot <- dplyr::mutate(
199:     paf_f,
200:     tstart_plot = dplyr::if_else(strand == "-", tend, tstart),
201:     tend_plot = dplyr::if_else(strand == "-", tstart, tend)
202:   )
203: 
204:   paf_plot <- dplyr::filter(paf_plot, qname == q_seq, tname == t_seq)
205:   if (nrow(paf_plot) == 0) {
206:     stop("No alignments found between '", q_seq, "' and '", t_seq, "'.")
207:   }
208: 
209:   ggplot2::ggplot(paf_plot) +
210:     ggplot2::geom_segment(
211:       ggplot2::aes(
212:         x = qstart, xend = qend,
213:         y = tstart_plot, yend = tend_plot,
214:         color = strand
215:       ),
216:       linewidth = 0.6
217:     ) +
218:     ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
219:       values = c("+" = "steelblue", "-" = "firebrick")
220:     ) +
221:     ggplot2::labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, title = title, color = "Strand") +
222:     ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
223:     ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())
224: }

(End of file - total 224 lines)
</content>

68: read_paf <- function(file) {
69:   # 12 mandatory PAF columns

## User
Now add this function as a new plot: #' Manhattan plot from snp table of stats
#'
#' @param data 
#' @param site 
#' @param today 
#' @param height 
#' @param width 
#' @param quick 
#' @param prefix 
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
plot_manhattan_by_site <- function(data, site, today, height, width, quick = F, save_pdf = T, prefix){

  print(site)

  print("Filter data to one site...")
  data <- data |>
    subset(SITE == site)

  if (quick){
    print("Subset insignificant data...")
    data <- data |>
      subset(pvalue < 0.001)
  }

  print("Compute variables...")
  don <- data %>%
    group_by(CHROM) %>%
    summarise(chr_len=max(POS)) %>%
    mutate(tot=cumsum(chr_len)-chr_len) %>%
    dplyr::select(-chr_len) %>%
    left_join(data, ., by=c("CHROM"="CHROM")) %>%
    arrange(CHROM, POS) %>%
    mutate(BPcum=POS+tot)

  axisdf = don %>%
    group_by(CHROM) %>%
    summarize(center=( max(BPcum) + min(BPcum) ) / 2 )

  print("Plot...")
  ggplot(don, aes(x=BPcum, y=-log10(pvalue))) +
    geom_point(aes(color=as.factor(CHROM)), alpha=0.8, size=1.3, shape = 16) +
    geom_point(data=subset(don, highlight=="yes"), color="orange", size=1.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = rep(c("grey", "black"), 22 )) +
    scale_x_continuous( label = axisdf$CHROM, breaks= axisdf$center ) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0) ) +
    theme(
      legend.position="none",
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()
    ) +
    labs(x = "Chromosome", y = "-log10(p)", title = paste("Site #", site, sep = " "))

  print("Save png...")
  ggsave(paste("../results/by-date/", today, "/", prefix, "_", site, ".jpg", sep = ""), height = height, width = width)

  if(save_pdf){
    print("Save pdf...")
    ggsave(paste("../results/by-date/", today, "/", prefix, "_", site, ".pdf", sep = ""), height = height, width = width)
  }
}

93: #' @param predictions Numeric vector of predicted values.

157: #' Dotplot of PAF alignments between two sequences
158: #'
159: #' Plots alignment blocks from a PAF data frame (as returned by [read_paf()])
160: #' as line segments: query coordinates on the x axis, target coordinates on
161: #' the y axis, colored by strand. Reverse-strand blocks are oriented so that
162: #' collinear alignments lie on a shared diagonal. Low-quality blocks can be
163: #' dropped via `min_alen`/`min_mapq`.
164: #'
165: #' @param paf A PAF data frame from [read_paf()].
166: #' @param q_seq Query sequence name to plot (`qname`).
167: #' @param t_seq Target sequence name to plot (`tname`).
168: #' @param xlab X-axis label (query).
169: #' @param ylab Y-axis label (target).
170: #' @param title Plot title.
171: #' @param min_alen Minimum alignment block length to plot (default 1000).
172: #' @param min_mapq Minimum mapping quality to plot (default 1).
173: #'
174: #' @return A ggplot object. Add highlights (e.g. [ggplot2::geom_hline()]) and
175: #'   save it with [save_plot()].
176: #' @export
177: #'
178: #' @examples
179: #' paf <- data.frame(
180: #'   qname = c("q1", "q1", "q1", "q2"),
181: #'   qlen = 10000, qstart = c(100, 500, 100, 100), qend = c(4000, 9000, 4000, 4000),
182: #'   strand = c("+", "+", "-", "+"),
183: #'   tname = c("t1", "t1", "t1", "t2"),
184: #'   tlen = 10000, tstart = c(200, 600, 700, 200),
185: #'   tend = c(5000, 10000, 10000, 5000),
186: #'   nmatch = c(3900, 4500, 3800, 2900),
187: #'   alen = c(3900, 4500, 4000, 3900),
188: #'   mapq = c(60, 60, 60, 0)
189: #' )
190: #' p <- plot_paf_dotplot(paf, q_seq = "q1", t_seq = "t1",
191: #'                       xlab = "Query q1", ylab = "Target t1",
192: #'                       title = "Demo dotplot")
193: plot_paf_dotplot <- function(paf, q_seq, t_seq, xlab, ylab, title,
194:                              min_alen = 1000, min_mapq = 1) {
195:   paf_f <- dplyr::filter(paf, alen >= min_alen, mapq >= min_mapq)
196: 
197:   # Orient reverse-strand alignments for correct diagonal direction
198:   paf_plot <- dplyr::mutate(
199:     paf_f,
200:     tstart_plot = dplyr::if_else(strand == "-", tend, tstart),
201:     tend_plot = dplyr::if_else(strand == "-", tstart, tend)
202:   )
203: 
204:   paf_plot <- dplyr::filter(paf_plot, qname == q_seq, tname == t_seq)
205:   if (nrow(paf_plot) == 0) {
206:     stop("No alignments found between '", q_seq, "' and '", t_seq, "'.")
207:   }
208: 
209:   ggplot2::ggplot(paf_plot) +
210:     ggplot2::geom_segment(
211:       ggplot2::aes(
212:         x = qstart, xend = qend,
213:         y = tstart_plot, yend = tend_plot,
214:         color = strand
215:       ),

## Plan: `plot_manhattan()` — GWAS Manhattan plot

Based on your answers (plot-only, optional `highlight` column, dplyr style):

### Design
- **Name**: `plot_manhattan` (not `plot_manhattan_by_site` — the `site` filter moves to the caller, per your "plot only" choice).
- **Signature**:
  ```r
  plot_manhattan(data, xlab = "Chromosome", ylab = "-log10(p)", title = NULL)
  ```
  Requires columns `CHROM`, `POS`, `pvalue` (your snp-table names, kept as-is). `highlight` (`"yes"`/other) is optional — orange overlay layer added only if the column exists.
- **Dropped**: `site`, `quick`, `today`, `prefix`, `save_pdf`, `height`, `width`, all `print()` chatter, both `ggsave()` calls. Caller: `data |> dplyr::filter(SITE == s) |> plot_manhattan() |> save_plot(...)`.

### Implementation (appended to `R/plotting.R` ~line 225, after `plot_paf_dotplot`)
1. Validate: informative `stop()` if `data` is empty or lacks required columns (same spirit as `plot_paf_dotplot`'s error).
2. Cumulative positions — same math as your script, rewritten with dplyr verbs (avoids the `%.%`-into-`left_join` pattern that breaks with `|>`):
   - `chr_bounds <- summarise(group_by(data, CHROM), chr_len = max(POS), .groups = "drop")`
   - `mutate(tot = cumsum(chr_len) - chr_len)`, then drop `chr_len` and `tot` after computing
   - `left_join(data, chr_bounds, by = "CHROM")`, `arrange(CHROM, POS)`, `mutate(BPcum = POS + tot)`
3. `axisdf` — per-chromosome `center = (max(BPcum) + min(BPcum)) / 2` (`.groups = "drop"`).
4. Plot (verbatim geometry from your script):

```r
#' Manhattan plot from a snp table
#'
#' Plots -log10(p) against cumulative genomic position for a table of SNP
#' statistics, with points colored by alternating chromosomes. If a
#' `highlight` column is present, rows with `highlight == "yes"` are drawn
#' again in orange on top.
#'
#' @param data A data frame of SNP statistics with columns `CHROM`, `POS`,
#'   `pvalue`, and optionally `highlight`.
#' @param xlab X-axis label.
#' @param ylab Y-axis label.
#' @param title Plot title.
#'
#' @return A ggplot object. Save it with [save_plot()].
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' set.seed(1)
#' snp_table <- data.frame(
#'   CHROM = rep(c("chr1", "chr2"), each = 500),
#'   POS = c(sample(1:1e6, 500), sample(1:8e5, 500)),
#'   pvalue = runif(1000)^5
#' )
#' snp_table$highlight <- ifelse(snp_table$pvalue < 1e-5, "yes", "no")
#' plot_manhattan(snp_table, title = "Example GWAS")
plot_manhattan <- function(data, xlab = "Chromosome", ylab = "-log10(p)", title = NULL) {
  required_cols <- c("CHROM", "POS", "pvalue")
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(data))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop("Missing required columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "), ".")
  }
  if (nrow(data) == 0) {
    stop("'data' has no rows.")
  }

  # Cumulative base-pair offset per chromosome
  chr_offsets <- dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::group_by(data, CHROM),
    chr_len = max(POS),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
  chr_offsets <- dplyr::mutate(
    chr_offsets,
    tot = cumsum(chr_len) - chr_len,
    chr_len = NULL
  )

  don <- dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::left_join(data, chr_offsets, by = "CHROM"),
    CHROM, POS
  )
  don <- dplyr::mutate(don, BPcum = POS + tot)

  axisdf <- dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::group_by(don, CHROM),
    center = (max(BPcum) + min(BPcum)) / 2,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(don, ggplot2::aes(x = BPcum, y = -log10(pvalue))) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      ggplot2::aes(color = as.factor(CHROM)),
      alpha = 0.8, size = 1.3, shape = 16
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
      values = rep(c("grey60", "black"), length.out = length(unique(don$CHROM)))
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = axisdf$CHROM, breaks = axisdf$center) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.border = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.x = ggplot2::element_blank()
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, title = title)

  if ("highlight" %in% names(data)) {
    p <- p +
      ggplot2::geom_point(
        data = dplyr::filter(don, highlight == "yes"),
        color = "orange", size = 1.5
      )
  }

  p
}
```

Add this function too: #' Plot heatmap from var-cov matrix
#'
#' @param covmat 
#' @param output_name 
#' @param include_values 
#' @param low_col 
#' @param mid_col 
#' @param high_col 
#' @param legend_name 
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
plot_var_cov_matrix <- function(covmat,
                                output_name,
                                include_values = TRUE,
                                low_col = "#65014B",
                                mid_col = "#F5F0F0",
                                high_col = "#0C4C00",
                                legend_name = "Cov(\u0394pi, \u0394pj)",
                                include_tick_labels = TRUE,
                                width = 7,
                                height = 7,
                                tile_or_raster = "tile",
                                discrete_or_continuous = "continuous") {
  
  upper_tri <- get_upper_tri(covmat)
  
  melted_cormat <- melt(upper_tri, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  plot_cor <- ggplot(data = melted_cormat, aes(Var2, Var1, fill = value))
  
  if (tile_or_raster == "tile") {
    plot_cor <- plot_cor + geom_tile(color = "white")
  } else if (tile_or_raster == "raster") {
    plot_cor <- plot_cor + geom_raster()
  } else {
    stop("tile_or_raster invalid.")
  }
  
  if (include_values) {
    plot_cor <- plot_cor + geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 4)),
                                     size = 5,
                                     color = "black")
  }
  
  if (discrete_or_continuous == "discrete") {
    plot_cor <- plot_cor + scale_fill_scico_d(
      palette = "bam",
      begin = 0.1,
      end = 0.9,
      name = legend_name
    )
  } else if (discrete_or_continuous == "continuous") {
    plot_cor <- plot_cor + scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = low_col,
      mid = mid_col,
      high = high_col,
      midpoint = 0,
      space = "Lab",
      name = legend_name
    )
  } else {
    stop("discrete_or_continuous invalid.")
  }
  
  plot_cor <- plot_cor + theme_minimal()
  
  if (include_tick_labels) {
    plot_cor <- plot_cor + theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 45,
        vjust = 1,
        hjust = 1
      ),
      text = element_text(size = 14, family = "Helvetica")
    )
  } else {
    plot_cor <- plot_cor +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), 
            axis.text.y = element_blank(),
            panel.background = element_blank(),
            panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
            panel.border = element_blank())
  }
  
  # remove axis names
  plot_cor <- plot_cor + coord_fixed() +
    labs(x = "", y = "")
  
  ggsave(
    output_name,
    plot_cor,
    bg = "white",
    device = cairo_pdf,
    width = width,
    height = height
  )
}

{

Cell values and/or tick labels can be suppressed for a\n#' publication-style matrix figure.\n#'\n#' @param covmat A square matrix with symmetric row and column names.\n#' @param include_values Print each cell's value (rounded to 4 decimals) on\n#'   its tile.\n#' @param include_tick_labels Show axis tick labels; if `FALSE`, all axis\n#'   text and panel decoration is removed.\n#' @param low_col Fill color for the most negative values.\n#' @param mid_col Fill color at the midpoint (0).\n#' @param high_col Fill color for the most positive values.\n#' @param legend_name Legend title.\n#' @param tile_or_raster `\"tile\"` (white cell borders) or `\"raster\"` (no\n#'   borders) geometry.\n#' @param discrete_or_continuous `\"continuous\"` uses a diverging color\n#'   gradient (`low_col`/`mid_col`/`high_col`); `\"discrete\"` uses the scico\n#'   `\"bam\"` palette (requires the scico package, a suggested dependency).\n#'\n#' @return A ggplot object. Save it with [save_plot()].\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' covmat <- matrix(\n#'   c(1.0, 0.3, 0.1,\n#'     0.3, 1.0, 0.5,\n#'     0.1, 0.5, 1.0),\n#'   nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE,\n#'   dimnames = list(c(\"s1\", \"s2\", \"s3\"), c(\"s1\", \"s2\", \"s3\"))\n#' )\n#' plot_var_cov_matrix(covmat, include_values = TRUE)\nplot_var_cov_matrix <- function(covmat,\n                                include_values = TRUE,\n                                include_tick_labels = TRUE,\n                                low_col = \"#65014B\",\n                                mid_col = \"#F5F0F0\",\n                                high_col = \"#0C4C00\",\n                                legend_name = \"Cov(\\u0394pi, \\u0394pj)\",\n                                tile_or_raster = c(\"tile\", \"raster\"),\n                                discrete_or_continuous = c(\"continuous\", \"discrete\")) {\n  tile_or_raster <- match.arg(tile_or_raster)\n  discrete_or_continuous <- match.arg(discrete_or_continuous)\n\n  if (!is.matrix(covmat) || nrow(covmat) != ncol(covmat)) {\n    stop(\"'covmat' must be a square matrix.\")\n  }\n  if (!identical(rownames(covmat), colnames(covmat))) {\n    stop(\"'covmat' must have identical row and column names.\")\n  }\n\n  upper_tri <- get_upper_tri(covmat)\n\n  # Long format in Var1/Var2/value columns, upper-triangle cells only,\n  # same semantics as reshape2::melt(..., na.rm = TRUE)\n  melted_cormat <- na.omit(as.data.frame.table(\n    upper_tri,\n    responseName = \"value\"\n  ))\n\n  plot_cor <- ggplot2::ggplot(melted_cormat, ggplot2::aes(Var2, Var1, fill = value))\n\n  if (tile_or_raster == \"tile\") {\n    plot_cor <- plot_cor + ggplot2::geom_tile(color = \"white\")\n  } else {\n    plot_cor <- plot_cor + ggplot2::geom_raster()\n  }\n\n  if (include_values) {\n    plot_cor <- plot_cor + ggplot2::geom_text(\n      ggplot2::aes(label = round(value, 4)),\n      size = 5,\n      color = \"black\"\n    )\n  }\n\n  if (discrete_or_continuous == \"discrete\") {\n    if (!requireNamespace(\"scico\", quietly = TRUE)) {\n      stop(\"The scico package is required for discrete_or_continuous = 'discrete'.\")\n    }\n    plot_cor <- plot_cor + scico::scale_fill_scico_d(\n      palette = \"bam\",\n      begin = 0.1,\n      end = 0.9,\n      name = legend_name\n    )\n  } else {\n    plot_cor <- plot_cor + ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(\n      low = low_col,\n      mid = mid_col,\n      high = high_col,\n      midpoint = 0,\n      space = \"Lab\",\n      name = legend_name\n    )\n  }\n\n  plot_cor <- plot_cor + ggplot2::theme_minimal()\n\n  if (include_tick_labels) {\n    plot_cor <- plot_cor + ggplot2::theme(\n      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(\n        angle = 45,\n        vjust = 1,\n        hjust = 1\n      ),\n      text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 14)\n    )\n  } else {\n    plot_cor <- plot_cor + ggplot2::theme(\n      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),\n      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),\n      panel.background = ggplot2::element_blank(),\n      panel.grid.major = ggplot2::element_blank(),\n      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),\n      panel.border = ggplot2::element_blank()\n    )\n  }\n\n  # ## Assistant (Build · GLM-5.3-Flash · 3.3s)

Found the root cause: the zeroed lower-triangle cells aren't `NA` — they're `0.0`, so `as.data.frame.table(..., na.omit)` can't drop them, and `p$data` ends up with all 9 cells (your script got 6 because `melt()` had set the zeros to `NA` via assignment on an `NA`-initialized matrix). Fixing the helper to match `melt` exactly — zero out the *lower triangle* by first filling with `NA`s:

**Tool: edit**

**Input:**
```json
{
  "filePath": "/home/miles/miles-rventures/R/plotting.R",
  "newString": "# Keep only the upper triangle of a square matrix: the strict lower triangle\n# becomes NA, so it drops out when melting (same as the reshape2::melt recipe\n# this function was ported from).\nget_upper_tri <- function(mat) {\n  mat[lower.tri(mat, diag = FALSE)] <- NA\n  mat\n}",
  "oldString": "# Zero out the lower triangle of a square matrix, so that only upper-triangle\n# cells remain for melting into a half-heatmap.\nget_upper_tri <- function(mat) {\n  mat[lower.tri(mat)] <- 0\n  mat\n}"
}
```

## User
Add these functions to the popgen module: #' Estimating standardized variance from allele frequencies
#'
#' @param p0 
#' @param pt 
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
fc <- function(p0, pt) {
  stopifnot(length(p0) == length(pt),
            all(p0 >= 0, na.rm = T),
            all(pt >= 0, na.rm = T),
            all(p0 <= 1, na.rm = T),
            all(pt <= 1, na.rm = T))
  
  #L <- length(p0)
  
  fsum_num <- (p0 - pt)^2
  
  #fsum_denom <- ((p0 + pt) / 2 - p0 * pt)
  fsum_denom <- p0*(1-p0)
  return(sum(fsum_num, na.rm = T)/sum(fsum_denom, na.rm = T))
  #return(fsum)
  #return(sum(fsum, na.rm = T) / sum(!is.nan(fsum)))
}

#' Estimate Ne, given estimate of N/Ne from selfing rate, Waples 1989
#'
#' @param s_low 
#' @param s_high 
#' @param Fc 
#' @param t 
#' @param S0 
#' @param St 
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
waples_ne <- function(r_low, r_high, p0, pt, S0, St, t){
  #r <- c(ncne(s_low), ncne(s_high))
  r <- c(r_low, r_high)
  Fc <- fc(p0, pt)
  ne <- (r*t - 2)/(2*r*(Fc - 1/(S0) - 1/(St)))
  return(ne)
}


#' Function to calculate LD decay distances, Hill and Weir 1988
#'
#' @param d distance between two loci in bp
#' @param n sample size
#' @param C Population-scaled recombination rate: 4Nc  
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
hill_weir_r2 <- function(d, n, C) {
  part1 <- (10 + C * d) / ((2 + C * d) * (11 + C * d))
  part2 <- 1 + ((3 + C * d) * (12 + 12 * C * d + (C * d) ^ 2)) / (n * (2 + C *
                                                                         d) * (11 + C * d))
  r2 <- part1 * part2
  return(r2)
}

{
  "filePath": "/home/miles/miles-rventures/R/popgen.R",
  "newString": "  counts <- numeric(G)\n  counts[1] <- N * q\n  for (i in 2:G) {\n    counts[i] <- stats::rbinom(1, N, fitfreq(counts[i - 1] / N, h, s[i - 1]))\n  }\n  counts / N\n}\n\n#' Standardized variance in allele-frequency change\n#'\n#' Estimates Fc, the standardized variance in allele-frequency change between\n#' two time points (Waples 1989): the sum of squared allele-frequency shifts\n#' across loci, normalized by the sum of `p0 * (1 - p0)` weighting terms.\n#'\n#' @param p0 Numeric vector of initial allele frequencies, in [0, 1].\n#' @param pt Numeric vector of allele frequencies after `t` generations,\n#'   same length as `p0`.\n#'\n#' @return A single numeric value, the standardized variance in allele\n#'   frequency change.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' fc(p0 = 0.5, pt = 0.25)\nfc <- function(p0, pt) {\n  stopifnot(\n    length(p0) == length(pt),\n    all(p0 >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),\n    all(pt >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),\n    all(p0 <= 1, na.rm = TRUE),\n    all(pt <= 1, na.rm = TRUE)\n  )\n\n  fsum_num <- (p0 - pt)^2\n  fsum_denom <- p0 * (1 - p0)\n\n  sum(fsum_num, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(fsum_denom, na.rm = TRUE)\n}\n\n#' Estimate Ne from the temporal method, corrected for selfing\n#'\n#' Applies the Waples (1989) correction for biased N/Ne estimates to convert\n#' an estimate of N/Ne derived from the selfing rate into an estimate of the\n#' effective population size Ne. Takes lower and upper bounds of the N/Ne\n#' ratio and returns the corresponding bounds of Ne, using the standardized\n#' variance in allele-frequency change computed with [fc()].\n#'\n#' @param r_low Lower bound of the N/Ne ratio estimated from the selfing rate.\n#' @param r_high Upper bound of the N/Ne ratio estimated from the selfing rate.\n#' @param p0 Numeric vector of initial allele frequencies, passed to [fc()].\n#' @param pt Numeric vector of final allele frequencies, passed to [fc()].\n#' @param S0 Sample size (number of diploid individuals) at time 0.\n#' @param St Sample size (number of diploid individuals) at time t.\n#' @param t Number of generations between the two samples.\n#'\n#' @return A numeric vector of length 2: Ne estimated with `r_low` and with\n#'   `r_high`.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' waples_ne(r_low = 2, r_high = 2, p0 = 0.5, pt = 0.25, S0 = 20, St = 20, t = 1)\nwaples_ne <- function(r_low, r_high, p0, pt, S0, St, t) {\n  r <- c(r_low, r_high)\n  Fc <- fc(p0, pt)\n  ne <- (r * t - 2) / (2 * r * (Fc - 1 / S0 - 1 / St))\n  return(ne)\n}\n\n#' Expected linkage disequilibrium between loci a given distance apart\n#'\n#' Computes the expected r^2 between two loci separated by distance `d`,\n#' accounting for finite sample size and population-scaled recombination\n#' rate (Hill and Weir 1988).\n#'\n#' @param d Distance between two loci in bp.\n#' @param n Sample size.\n#' @param C Population-scaled recombination rate: 4Nc.\n#'\n#' @return The expected r^2.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' hill_weir_r2(d = 1000, n = 30, C = 0.001)\n#' hill_weir_r2(d = c(0, 1000, 10000), n = 30, C = 0.001)\nhill_weir_r2 <- function(d, n, C) {\n  part1 <- (10 + C * d) / ((2 + C * d) * (11 + C * d))\n  part2 <- 1 + ((3 + C * d) * (12 + 12 * C * d + (C * d)^2)) /\n    (n * (2 + C * d) * (11 + C * d))\n  r2 <- part1 * part2\n  return(r2)\n}",
  "oldString": "  counts <- numeric(G)\n  counts[1] <- N * q\n  for (i in 2:G) {\n    counts[i] <- stats::rbinom(1, N, fitfreq(counts[i - 1] / N, h, s[i - 1]))\n  }\n  counts / N\n}"
}

#'
#' @param my_vector 
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
geom_pairwise_mean <- function(my_vector) {
  stopifnot(length(my_vector)>1, is.numeric(my_vector))
  n <- length(my_vector)
  var_sum <- 0
  for (i in 1:(n - 1)) {
    var_a <- my_vector[i]
    for (j in (i + 1):n) {
      var_b <- my_vector[j]
      var_sum <- var_sum + sqrt(var_a*var_b)
    }
  }
  var_mean <- var_sum/((n^2 - n)/2)
  return(var_mean)
}

#' Calculate convergence correlation within environment
#'
#' @param pdiff frequency increments for all replicates of one site, one time point
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
conv_cor_wn_env <- function(pdiff){
  stopifnot(ncol(pdiff) > 1, nrow(pdiff) > 1)
  covmat <- cov(pdiff, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  rep_var <- diag(covmat)
  rep_cov <- covmat[upper.tri(covmat)]
  numerator <- sum(2*rep_cov, na.rm = T)/(2*length(rep_cov))
  denominator <- geom_pairwise_mean(rep_var)
  stopifnot(denominator > 0, abs(numerator) <= denominator)
  return(c(numerator,denominator))
}


#' Replicate G(t): proportion of variance in dp due to shared selection pressure
#'
#' @param pdiff 
#' @param rep_labels 
#' @param time_labels 
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
replicate_gt <- function(pdiff, rep_labels, time_labels){
  
  stopifnot(ncol(pdiff) > 1, 
            nrow(pdiff) > 1, 
            length(rep_labels) == ncol(pdiff), 
            length(time_labels) == ncol(pdiff),
            length(unique(rep_labels)) >= 2,
            length(unique(time_labels)) >= 2)
  
  rep_eq_bool_mat <- outer(rep_labels, rep_labels, "==")
  
  time_eq_bool_mat <- outer(time_labels, time_labels, "==")
  
  covmat <- cov(pdiff, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  
  # total variance within replicates
  var_only_mat <- covmat[rep_eq_bool_mat]
  total_var <- sum(var_only_mat)
  total_var_pos <- sum(var_only_mat[(var_only_mat > 0)])
  total_var_abs <- sum(abs(var_only_mat))
  var_trace <- covmat[(rep_eq_bool_mat & time_eq_bool_mat)]
  total_var_trace <- sum(var_trace)
  n_var <- length(unique(rep_labels))
  
  # total covariance across different replicates AND time points
  cov_only_mat <- covmat[(!rep_eq_bool_mat) & (!time_eq_bool_mat)]
  total_covar <- sum(cov_only_mat)
  total_covar_abs <- sum(abs(cov_only_mat))
  total_covar_pos <- sum(cov_only_mat[(cov_only_mat > 0)])
  n_covar <- (n_var^2 - n_var)/2
  
  mean_var = total_var/n_var
  mean_var_pos = total_var_pos/n_var
  mean_var_abs = total_var_abs/n_var
  mean_var_trace = total_var_trace/n_var
  mean_covar = total_covar/n_covar
  mean_covar_pos = total_covar_pos/n_covar
  mean_covar_abs = total_covar_abs/n_covar
  
  stopifnot(total_covar <= total_covar_pos,
            mean_covar <= mean_covar_pos,
            total_var_pos <= total_var_abs,
            total_covar < sum(abs(covmat)), 
            total_var < sum(abs(covmat)),
            total_covar <= total_covar_abs,
            all.equal(sum(var_only_mat)+sum(covmat[!rep_eq_bool_mat]), 
                      sum(covmat)),
            mean_var >= 0, 
            total_var >= 0,
            total_var_trace >= 0,
            mean_var_trace >= 0)
  
  return(data.frame(
    mean_var = mean_var,
    mean_var_pos = mean_var_pos,
    mean_var_abs = mean_var_abs,
    mean_var_trace = mean_var_trace,
    mean_covar = mean_covar,
    mean_covar_pos = mean_covar_pos,
    mean_covar_abs = mean_covar_abs,
    total_var = total_var,
    total_var_pos = total_var_pos,
    total_var_abs = total_var_abs,
    total_var_trace = total_var_trace,
    total_covar = total_covar,
    total_covar_pos = total_covar_pos,
    total_covar_abs = total_covar_abs,
    n_var = n_var,
    n_covar = n_covar
  ))

}


#' Rolling sum of matrix, starting from top left, sum matrix elements in nested squares
#'
#' @param mat 
#'
#' @return 
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
rolling_matrix_sum <- function(mat){
  stopifnot(nrow(mat) == ncol(mat))
  rolling_sum <- c()
  for(i in 1:ncol(mat)){
    rolling_sum <- c(rolling_sum, sum(mat[1:i,1:i]))
  }
  stopifnot(length(rolling_sum) == ncol(mat))
  return(rolling_sum)
}

#' G statistic, corrected for selection increasing variance in allele frequency change
#'
#' @param t 
#' @param p0 
#' @param N 
#' @param pmat 
#' @param n 
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
g_prime <- function(times, pmat, N, n, take_abs = F){
  stopifnot(all(times >= 0), N > 2)
  covmat <- covmat_from_pmat(pmat, n)
  ep0 <- mean(pmat[,1]*(1-pmat[,1]), na.rm = T)
  if(take_abs){
    var_roll <- rolling_matrix_sum(abs(covmat))
  } else {
    var_roll <- rolling_matrix_sum(covmat)
  }
  stopifnot(length(times) == length(var_roll))
  return(1 - (times*ep0)/(2*N*var_roll))
} #' Calculate covariances from allele frequency matrix
#'
#' @param pmat matrix of allele frequencies, first column is initial generation
#' @param n optional, vector of sample size, number of chromosomes by site
#' @param correct_for_n boolean, whether to correct for sample size
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
covmat_from_pmat <- function(pmat, n = NULL, correct_for_n = T, standard_by_het = F, input_asin_trans = F, procedure = "none", windows = NULL){
  # allele frequency changes between adjacent generations
  pdiff <- freq_increments(pmat)
  # randomly swap signs of allele frequency changes
  pdiff <- sign_permute_increments(pdiff, procedure = procedure, windows = windows)
  # ensure pdiff is a matrix even with a single increment (2-column pmat)
  if(is.null(dim(pdiff))){
    pdiff <- matrix(pdiff, ncol = 1)
  }
  # covariance matrices
  covmat <- stats::cov(pdiff, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  # correct for sample size, if needed
  if(correct_for_n){
    if(any(n < 2)){
      stop("All n must be >= 2")
    }
    if(length(n) != (ncol(covmat) + 1)){
      stop("Should be a sample size for every time point.")
    }
    ### ARCSIN SQRT TRANSFORMED FREQUENCIES ###
    if(input_asin_trans){
      # check transformed data are actually input
      if(all(pmat[,1] < pi)){
        warning("Are you sure values are arcsin transformed?")
      }
      # correct overlapping covariances
      # seq_len() yields integer(0) when ncol(covmat) == 1, so this is skipped
      for(i in seq_len(ncol(covmat) - 1)){
        corrected_cov <- covmat[i,i+1] + (1/n[i+1])
        covmat[i,i+1] <- corrected_cov
        covmat[i+1,i] <- corrected_cov
      }
      # correct variances
      for(i in seq_len(ncol(covmat))){
        corrected_var <- covmat[i,i] - (1/n[i]) - (1/n[i+1])
        if(corrected_var < 0) {
          print("Sample size correction makes variance negative. Setting variance to zero")
          covmat[i,i] <- 0
        } else{
          covmat[i,i] <- corrected_var
        }
      }
      ###RAW FREQUENCIES###
    } else {
      # correct overlapping covariances
      # seq_len() yields integer(0) when ncol(covmat) == 1, so this is skipped
      for(i in seq_len(ncol(covmat) - 1)){
        corrected_cov <- mean(pdiff[,i] * pdiff[,i+1], na.rm = T) + mean(pmat[,i+1]*(1-pmat[,i+1])/(n[i+1] - 1), na.rm = T)
        covmat[i,i+1] <- corrected_cov
        covmat[i+1,i] <- corrected_cov
      }
      # correct variances
      for(i in seq_len(ncol(covmat))){
        corrected_var <- mean((pdiff[,i])^2, na.rm = T) - mean(pmat[,i]*(1-pmat[,i])/(n[i] - 1), na.rm = T) - mean(pmat[,i+1]*(1-pmat[,i+1])/(n[i+1] - 1), na.rm = T)
        if( corrected_var < 0 | is.na(corrected_var) ) {
          print("Sample size correction makes variance negative. Setting variance to zero")
          covmat[i,i] <- 0
        } else{
          covmat[i,i] <- corrected_var
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  if(standard_by_het){
    covmat <- standard_cov_by_het(pmat[,-ncol(pmat), drop = FALSE], covmat)
  }
  
  return(covmat)
} #' Allele frequency changes between adjacent generations
#'
#' @param pmat matrix of allele frequencies, timepoints ascending from left column to right column
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
freq_increments <- function(pmat){
  pmat[, -1] - pmat[, -ncol(pmat)]
}


#' Standardize covmat by 
#'
#' @param pmat excluding the last time point
#' @param covmat 
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
standard_cov_by_het <- function(pmat, covmat) {
  stopifnot(ncol(pmat) == ncol(covmat))
  half_het_sums <- 0.5*apply(pmat, MARGIN = 2, FUN = sum_of_het)
  stopifnot(all(half_het_sums > 0))
  # standaridize variances
  diag(covmat) <- diag(covmat)/half_het_sums
  # standardize covariances
  for(i in 1:nrow(covmat)){
    for(j in 1:ncol(covmat)){
      if(i != j){
        covmat[i,j] <- covmat[i,j]/half_het_sums[min(c(i,j))]
      }
    }
  }
  return(covmat)
} #' Calculate linked selection ratios from covariance matrix
#'
#' @param covmat 
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
gt_from_covmat <- function(covmat) {
  covmat[lower.tri(covmat)] <- NA

  covariances <- covmat[upper.tri(covmat)]
  variances <- diag(covmat)

  sums_var <- cumsum(variances)

  sums_cov = c(0)
  sums_abs_cov = c(0)
  sums_pos_cov = c(0)
  sums_neg_cov = c(0)
  for(j in 2:nrow(covmat)){
    cov_sub <- covariances[1:(((j-1)*(j))/2)]

    sum_abs_cov <- 2*sum(abs(cov_sub), na.rm = T)
    sum_cov <- 2*sum(cov_sub, na.rm = T)
    sum_neg_cov <- 2*sum(abs(cov_sub[(cov_sub < 0)]), na.rm = T)
    sum_pos_cov <- 2*sum(cov_sub[(cov_sub > 0)], na.rm = T)

    sums_cov = c(sums_cov, sum_cov)
    sums_abs_cov = c(sums_abs_cov, sum_abs_cov)
    sums_pos_cov = c(sums_pos_cov, sum_pos_cov)
    sums_neg_cov = c(sums_neg_cov, sum_neg_cov)
  }

  result = data.frame(
    gen = 1:nrow(covmat),
    gt = sums_cov/(sums_var + sums_cov),
    gt_abs = sums_abs_cov/(sums_var + sums_abs_cov),
    gt_abs_2 = sums_abs_cov/(sums_var + sums_cov),
    gt_pos = sums_pos_cov/(sums_var + sums_pos_cov),
    sum_cov = sums_cov,
    sum_abs_cov = sums_abs_cov,
    sum_pos_cov = sums_pos_cov,
    sum_neg_cov = sums_neg_cov,
    sum_var = sums_var,
    ratio = sums_pos_cov/(sums_pos_cov + sums_neg_cov)
  )
  return(result)
} #' Sum of heterozygosity 
#'
#' @param x vector of allele frequencies, one per locus
#'
#' @return single number
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
sum_of_het <- function(x){
  sum(2*x*(1-x), na.rm = T)
} #' Calculate covariances across a pair of environments
#'
#' @param pmat1 matrix of allele frequencies in population 1, rows = variants, columns = replicates
#' @param pmat2 matrix of allele frequencies in population 2, rows = variants, columns = replicates
#' @param pop1 
#' @param pop2 
#' @param gen0 
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
covmat_pop_pair <- function(pmat1, pmat2, pop1, pop2, gen0){
  # allele frequency changes between adjacent generations
  pdiff1 <- pmat1 - gen0
  pdiff2 <- pmat2 - gen0
  
  covmat <- cov(cbind(pdiff1, pdiff2), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  
  # mean product of std of between population pairs
  rep_var <- diag(covmat)
  rep_var_1 <- rep_var[1:ncol(pmat1)]
  rep_var_2 <- rep_var[(ncol(pmat1) + 1):length(rep_var)]
  mean_pair_std <- mean(sqrt(rep_var_1 %o% rep_var_2))
  
  bw_pop_cov <- covmat[grep(pop1, rownames(covmat)), grep(pop2, colnames(covmat))]
  
  return(mean(bw_pop_cov)/mean_pair_std)
}

User has answered your questions: "covmat_from_pmat() calls sign_permute_increments(pdiff, procedure = procedure, windows = windows), but that function wasn't in your paste. How should I handle it?"="#' Sign permute a block of allele frequencies
#'
#' @param pdiff 
#' @param procedure 
#' @param windows 
#'
#' @returns
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
sign_permute_increments <- function(pdiff, procedure = "none", windows = NULL){
  stopifnot(ncol(pdiff)>=2, nrow(pdiff)>=2)
  if(procedure == "window"){
    # within a window, randomly multiply allele frequency change by +1 or -1
    pdiff$window <- windows
    pdiff <- pdiff %>%
      group_by(window) %>%
      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ .x * sample(c(1, -1), size = 1))) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::select(-window) %>%
      as.data.frame()
  } else if (procedure == "cell"){
    # randomly multiply every cell frequency change by +1 or -1
    pdiff <- pdiff %>%
      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ .x * sample(c(1, -1), n(), replace = TRUE)))
  } else if (procedure == "genome"){
    # randomly multiply entire columns by +1 or -1
    sign_permutations <- sample(c(-1,1), size = ncol(pdiff), replace = T)
    # Create the diagonal matrix from vector
    P <- diag(sign_permutations)
    # Perform matrix multiplication to flip all increments at once
    pdiff <- as.matrix(pdiff) %*% P
  } else if (procedure == "none") {
    # no flipping
  }
  else {
    stop("Procedure not valid. Choose from list of options.")
  }
  return(pdiff)
}", "For the four dataset structures (LxS allele-frequency matrix, Lx2 chr/pos, Lx1 initial freqs, Sx3 sample metadata), how much machinery do you want?"="Full S3 kit (Recommended)", "Names for the four constructors (S3 class = constructor name, standard R style)?"="freq_matrix, snp_coords, p0_vec, sample_info", "covmat_pop_pair() needs column names containing the population label (it greps them), and replicate_gt() needs rep/time labels from the metadata. validate_af_dataset(fm, sc, pv, si): checks
- inherits all four
- nrow(fm) == nrow(sc) == length(pv) >= 1
- ncol(fm) == nrow(si)
- si columns: population, time_point, replicate (integer)
- optionally: if fm has colnames, they match paste(si$population, si$time_point, si$replicate, sep="_")? Should colnames be REQUIRED to match? extract_samples builds them that way. Validator could check only if colnames present. I'll check: if !is.null(colnames(fm)), expect them to equal built names (warn/stop?). Make it an error if mismatch — strict. Hmm, but users may construct freq_matrix with arbitrary colnames. The validator is opt-in; strictness OK. I'll include the check as error. Or make it a separate check in extract_samples only. Keep validator checks to dims/types; put the colname-matching check in validator too but only when colnames present. Fine.

extract_samples(fm, si, population = NULL, time = NULL, replicate = NULL):
- validate fm is freq_matrix, si is sample_info, ncol(fm) == nrow(si)
- build logical mask over columns; error if no columns selected ("No samples match...")
- subset matrix, drop=FALSE
- colnames <- paste(pop, time, rep, sep = "_") for selected

covmat_pop_pair port:
```r
covmat_pop_pair <- function(pmat1, pmat2, pop1, pop2, gen0) {
  pdiff1 <- pmat1 - gen0
  pdiff2 <- pmat2 - gen0
  covmat <- stats::cov(cbind(pdiff1, pdiff2), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  rep_var <- diag(covmat)
  rep_var_1 <- rep_var[seq_len(ncol(pmat1))]
  rep_var_2 <- rep_var[(ncol(pmat1) + 1):length(rep_var)]
  mean_pair_std <- mean(sqrt(rep_var_1 %o% rep_var_2))
  bw_pop_cov <- covmat[base::grep(pop1, rownames(covmat)), base::grep(pop2, colnames(covmat))]
  mean(bw_pop_cov) / mean_pair_std
}
```

## Plan — popgen temporal-replicates toolkit + dataset kit

### A. Dataset kit (new, at top of `R/popgen.R`; ~10 objects)

Constructors validate + attach an S3 class (plain matrix/df/vector underneath, so all downstream numeric code just works):

| Constructor | Input → validation | Class |
|---|---|---|
| `freq_matrix(x)` | numeric **L×S matrix**, all values in [0,1] (NA allowed); dimnames preserved | `"freq_matrix"` |
| `snp_coords(x)` | **L×2 data.frame** with columns `CHROM` (character) / `POS` (numeric, no NA) — uppercase to interop with `plot_manhattan()` | `"snp_coords"` |
| `p0_vec(x)` | numeric vector (single-col matrix accepted → coerced), in [0,1] | `"p0_vec"` |
| `sample_info(x)` | **S×3 data.frame** with columns `population`, `time_point`, `replicate`; coerced to character/integer/character, no NAs, time ≥ 0 | `"sample_info"` |

Plus:
- `print()` methods for all four (dim summary + head; exported, own roxygen blocks).
- `validate_af_dataset(freq_mat, snp_coords, p0, sample_meta)` — cross-checks `nrow(fm) == nrow(coords) == length(p0)` (L) and `ncol(fm) == nrow(sample_meta)` (S); if `fm` has colnames, checks they match the `pop_time_rep` scheme.
- `extract_samples(freq_mat, sample_meta, population = NULL, time = NULL, replicate = NULL)` — subsets columns (any combination, `%in%` matching), errors if nothing matches, rebuilds colnames as `pop_time_rep` (so `covmat_pop_pair()`'s `grep()` works), attaches the subset `sample_meta` as attribute `"sample_info"`, returns classed `freq_matrix`.

### B. Ported functions (order respects dependencies)

`sum_of_het` → `geom_pairwise_mean` → `freq_increments` → `sign_permute_increments` → `standard_cov_by_het` → `covmat_from_pmat` → `rolling_matrix_sum` → `g_prime` → `gt_from_covmat` → `conv_cor_wn_env` → `replicate_gt` → `covmat_pop_pair`. Logic, loops, and comments ported as-is with these flagged deviations:

1. **`sign_permute_increments`**: your paste assumes `pdiff` is a data.frame, but `freq_increments()` returns a matrix — I'll coerce to data.frame for the `window`/`cell` dplyr branches (`dplyr::` namespaced, sequential calls instead of `%>%` so no magrittr/native-pipe dependency). Add `stopifnot(!is.null(windows), length(windows) == nrow(pdiff))` for the window branch, and the invalid-procedure error will name the valid options.
2. **Relaxed check**: `stopifnot(ncol(pdiff) >= 2)` → `>= 1`, otherwise `covmat_from_pmat()`'s documented 2-timepoint path (the `is.null(dim(pdiff))` guard + `seq_len` comments) is unreachable dead code.
3. **`covmat_from_pmat`**: `print("Sample size correction...")` → `warning(...)` (2 sites); `T` → `TRUE`.
4. **`g_prime`**: roxygen rewritten to the *actual* signature `(times, pmat, N, n, take_abs = FALSE)` (your doc block describes an older `(t, p0, N, pmat, n)`).
5. **`standard_cov_by_het`**: finish the truncated title ("Standardize covariance matrix by heterozygosity"); document that `pmat` = frequencies at the *start* of each interval (`pmat[, -ncol(pmat)]`).
6. **`covmat_pop_pair`**: add `stopifnot(!is.null(colnames(pmat1)), !is.null(colnames(pmat2)))` (grep silently returns empty on NULL names otherwise); `stats::cov`, `base::grep`.

All get roxygen with runnable `@examples` (small hand-built matrices; `set.seed` for sign-permutation examples).

### C. Tests (append to `tests/testthat/test-popgen.R`)

- **Kit**: constructors class + validation errors (out-of-range freqs, wrong-shape coords, wrong-named/col-count sample_info); `print` output via `expect_output`; `validate_af_dataset` pass + L-mismatch + S-mismatch errors; `extract_samples` dims/colnames/filters/no-match error.
- **Arithmetic**: `geom_pairwise_mean` hand values (n=2, n=3) + errors; `freq_increments` hand values; `sum_of_het` + NA skip; `rolling_matrix_sum` on `matrix(1:9,3)` → `c(1,12,45)` + non-square error.
- **`sign_permute_increments`**: `"none"` unchanged; `"genome"` = column-flip (compare to manual `diag(signs)` multiply under `set.seed`); `"cell"` preserves absolute values; `"window"` = one sign per window×column (verify within-block constancy); invalid procedure error.
- **`covmat_from_pmat`**: `procedure="none", correct_for_n=FALSE` equals `stats::cov(freq_increments(pmat))`; hand-computed sample-size-corrected variance/covariance (raw branch) incl. exact match; negative-variance → warning + diag 0 (n=2, identical columns); asin-branch warning on plain frequencies; `n < 2` and wrong-length `n` errors; 2-timepoint input works (relaxation).
- **`standard_cov_by_het`**: hand-check var/`half_het` and cov/`half_het[min(i,j)]` rules.
- **`g_prime`**: replicate the corrected-covmat + rolling-sum + formula inline for an exact match; closer to 1 with larger N; `take_abs = TRUE` differs; `times` length mismatch error.
- **`gt_from_covmat`** on a hand 3×3: `gt[1] == 0`, gen-2/gen-3 closed forms, `gt_abs`, `ratio`.
- **`conv_cor_wn_env`**: exact numerator/denominator; degenerate zero-variance → error.
- **`replicate_gt`**: L×4 hand case, verify `mean_var`, `total_covar`, `n_var = 2`, `n_covar = 1` etc.; label-length + <2-unique errors.
- **`covmat_pop_pair`**: hand-computed ratio on 4×4 block covmat.
- **Integration**: build a synthetic 2 pops × 3 times × 2 reps, L=15 dataset via all four constructors → `validate_af_dataset()` → `extract_samples()` feeds `freq_increments`/`covmat_from_pmat`/`g_prime`, two-pop `covmat_pop_pair`, and `replicate_gt` with metadata-derived labels.

### D. Verify + ship

1. `devtools::document()` → ~15 new `.Rd`, NAMESPACE exports.
2. `devtools::test()` → expect `FAIL 0 | WARN 1 | PASS ~110` (the one pre-existing `write.table` warning).
3. `devtools::check()` on sanitized temp copy → expect the 2 known NOTEs.
4. Commit `feat: add temporal-replicates popgen functions and dataset kit` — **no push** (say "push" and I will).

**Assumption to veto if wrong:** `snp_coords` uses uppercase `CHROM`/`POS` so the Lx2 object plugs directly into `plot_manhattan()`; `extract_samples` gains an optional `replicate =` filter (beyond the population/time you approved) since it's needed to slice single-replicate `pmat`s for `covmat_from_pmat()`.

#'
#' @param x time series of allele frequences, assumed ordered from 0, 1, 2,..., t
#'
#' @return

#'

rm_na_after_na <- function(x){
  y <- which(is.na(x))
  if(length(y) > 0){
    first_na <- min(y) # get first na in sequence
    x[first_na:length(x)] <- NA # mark instances after first na as also na
  }
  return(x)

23: #'
24: #' Simulates a Wright-Fisher trajectory of a biallelic locus under selection
25: #' and genetic drift. Each generation, the deterministic allele frequency
26: #' after selection is computed with [fitfreq()], then the number of A alleles
27: #' in the next generation is drawn from a binomial distribution.

43: WF_sel <- function(N, q, h, s, G) {
44:   if (length(s) == 1) {
45:     s <- rep(s, G - 1)
46:   } else if (length(s) != G - 1) {
47:     stop("s must be a scalar or a vector of length G - 1.")
48:   }
49: 
50:   counts <- numeric(G)
51:   counts[1] <- N * q
52:   for (i in 2:G) {
53:     counts[i] <- stats::rbinom(1, N, fitfreq(counts[i - 1] / N, h, s[i - 1]))
54:   }
55:   counts / N
56: }

60: #' Estimates Fc, the standardized variance in allele-frequency change between

62: #' across loci, normalized by the sum of `p0 * (1 - p0)` weighting terms.
63: #'
64: #' @param p0 Numeric vector of initial allele frequencies, between 0 and 1.
65: #' @param pt Numeric vector of allele frequencies after `t` generations,
66: #'   same length as `p0`.
67: #'
68: #' @return A single numeric value, the standardized variance in allele
69: #'   frequency change.
70: #' @export
71: #'
72: #' @examples
73: #' fc(p0 = 0.5, pt = 0.25)
74: fc <- function(p0, pt) {
75:   stopifnot(
76:     length(p0) == length(pt),
77:     all(p0 >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
78:     all(pt >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
79:     all(p0 <= 1, na.rm = TRUE),
80:     all(pt <= 1, na.rm = TRUE)

82: 
83:   fsum_num <- (p0 - pt)^2
84:   fsum_denom <- p0 * (1 - p0)

94: #' ratio and returns the corresponding bounds of Ne, using the standardized

113: waples_ne <- function(r_low, r_high, p0, pt, S0, St, t) {
114:   r <- c(r_low, r_high)

116:   ne <- (r * t - 2) / (2 * r * (Fc - 1 / S0 - 1 / St))
