  "newString": "  attr(out, \"sample_info\") <- sub_meta\n  class(out) <- c(\"freq_matrix\", class(out))\n  out\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Temporal-replicate popgen: frequency changes, covariance, and G statistics\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Sum of heterozygosity\n#'\n#' Computes `sum(2 * x * (1 - x))` over a vector of allele frequencies, one\n#' per locus, skipping NAs.\n#'\n#' @param x Numeric vector of allele frequencies, one per locus.\n#'\n#' @return A single number: the summed heterozygosity.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' sum_of_het(c(0.5, 0.25, 1))\nsum_of_het <- function(x) {\n  sum(2 * x * (1 - x), na.rm = TRUE)\n}\n\n#' Pairwise geometric mean\n#'\n#' Computes the mean of `sqrt(x_i * x_j)` over all unordered pairs of\n#' elements in a numeric vector.\n#'\n#' @param my_vector Numeric vector of length at least 2.\n#'\n#' @return A single number: the mean of the pairwise geometric means.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' geom_pairwise_mean(c(1, 4, 9))\ngeom_pairwise_mean <- function(my_vector) {\n  stopifnot(length(my_vector) > 1, is.numeric(my_vector))\n  n <- length(my_vector)\n  var_sum <- 0\n  for (i in 1:(n - 1)) {\n    var_a <- my_vector[i]\n    for (j in (i + 1):n) {\n      var_b <- my_vector[j]\n      var_sum <- var_sum + sqrt(var_a * var_b)\n    }\n  }\n  var_mean <- var_sum / ((n^2 - n) / 2)\n  return(var_mean)\n}\n\n#' Allele frequency changes between adjacent generations\n#'\n#' Computes the differences between adjacent columns of an allele frequency\n#' matrix: columns are time points in ascending order, rows are variants.\n#'\n#' @param pmat Numeric matrix of allele frequencies; time points ascending\n#'   from the left column to the right column.\n#'\n#' @return A numeric matrix with the same number of rows and one fewer\n#'   column than `pmat`: the allele frequency change in each interval.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' pmat <- matrix(c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)\n#' freq_increments(pmat)\nfreq_increments <- function(pmat) {\n  pmat[, -1] - pmat[, -ncol(pmat)]\n}\n\n#' Mark entries after first NA as also NA\n#'\n#' Given a time series of allele frequencies ordered from time 0, 1, 2, ...,\n#' t, sets every entry from the first NA onward to NA, truncating the\n#' trajectory at its first missing value.\n#'\n#' @param x Numeric vector assumed to be ordered in time.\n#'\n#' @return The input vector with all entries from the first NA onward set\n#'   to NA. Unchanged if there is no NA.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' rm_na_after_na(c(0.1, 0.2, NA, 0.4, 0.5))\nrm_na_after_na <- function(x) {\n  y <- which(is.na(x))\n  if (length(y) > 0) {\n    first_na <- min(y) # get first na in sequence\n    x[first_na:length(x)] <- NA # mark instances after first na as also na\n  }\n  return(x)\n}\n\n#' Arcsine-square root transform of allele frequencies\n#'\n#' Applies the variance-stabilizing arcsine-square root transformation,\n#' `asin(sqrt(x))`, commonly used before temporal analyses of allele\n#' frequencies.\n#'\n#' @param x Numeric vector of values in \\code{[0, 1]}; NA entries pass\n#'   through as NA.\n#'\n#' @return The transformed numeric vector, in \\code{[0, pi/2]}.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' arcsin_sqrt(c(0, 0.5, 1))\narcsin_sqrt <- function(x) {\n  stopifnot(\n    is.numeric(x),\n    all(x >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),\n    all(x <= 1, na.rm = TRUE)\n  )\n  asin(sqrt(x))\n}\n\n#' Sign permute a block of allele frequency changes\n#'\n#' Randomly multiplies allele frequency changes by +1 or -1 at one of several\n#' granularities, for use in randomization tests of linked selection.\n#' Because covariance is signed, flipping signs breaks real shared-direction\n#' structure while preserving per-element magnitudes.\n#'\n#' @param pdiff Data.frame or matrix of allele frequency changes (rows =\n#'   variants, columns = time intervals).\n#' @param procedure One of `\"none\"` (return input unchanged), `\"window\"`\n#'   (one random sign per genomic window, applied to all variants in the\n#'   window), `\"cell\"` (one random sign per matrix entry), or `\"genome\"`\n#'   (one random sign per column). Invalid values raise an error.\n#' @param windows Numeric or character vector of window IDs, one per row of\n#'   `pdiff`; required when `procedure = \"window\"`.\n#'\n#' @return The sign-permuted allele frequency changes, as a data.frame for\n#'   procedures `\"window\"` and `\"cell\"` and a matrix for `\"genome\"` and\n#'   `\"none\"`.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' set.seed(1)\n#' pdiff <- data.frame(d1 = c(-0.1, 0.2, -0.3, 0.4), d2 = c(0.1, -0.2, 0.3, -0.4))\n#' sign_permute_increments(pdiff, procedure = \"genome\")\nsign_permute_increments <- function(pdiff, procedure = \"none\", windows = NULL) {\n  stopifnot(ncol(pdiff) >= 1, nrow(pdiff) >= 1)\n  pdiff <- as.data.frame(pdiff)\n  if (procedure == \"window\") {\n    # within a window, randomly multiply allele frequency change by +1 or -1\n    stopifnot(!is.null(windows), length(windows) == nrow(pdiff))\n    pdiff$window <- windows\n    pdiff <- dplyr::group_by(pdiff, window)\n    pdiff <- dplyr::mutate(\n      pdiff, dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), ~ .x * sample(c(1, -1), size = 1))\n    )\n    pdiff <- dplyr::ungroup(pdiff)\n    pdiff <- pdiff[, setdiff(names(pdiff), \"window\"), drop = FALSE]\n  } else if (procedure == \"cell\") {\n    # randomly multiply every cell frequency change by +1 or -1\n    pdiff <- dplyr::mutate(\n      pdiff, dplyr::across(\n        dplyr::where(is.numeric), ~ .x * sample(c(1, -1), n(), replace = TRUE)\n      )\n    )\n  } else if (procedure == \"genome\") {\n    # randomly multiply entire columns by +1 or -1\n    sign_permutations <- sample(c(-1, 1), size = ncol(pdiff), replace = TRUE)\n    # Create the diagonal matrix from vector\n    P <- diag(sign_permutations)\n    # Perform matrix multiplication to flip all increments at once\n    pdiff <- as.matrix(pdiff) %*% P\n  } else if (procedure == \"none\") {\n    # no flipping\n    pdiff <- as.matrix(pdiff)\n  } else {\n    stop(\"Procedure not valid. Choose from: none, window, cell, genome.\")\n  }\n  return(pdiff)\n}\n\n#' Standardize covariance matrix by heterozygosity\n#'\n#' Divides each variance and covariance of a temporal covariance matrix by\n#' the summed heterozygosity of the corresponding interval, so that entries\n#' are comparable across intervals with different amounts of standing\n#' variation. Covariances are divided by `half_het_sums[min(i, j)]`, the\n#' heterozygosity of the earlier of the two intervals.\n#'\n#' @param pmat Numeric matrix of allele frequencies excluding the last time\n#'   point: one column per interval, holding the frequencies at the start of\n#'   that interval.\n#' @param covmat Square covariance matrix of allele frequency changes, with\n#'   one row/column per interval.\n#'\n#' @return The standardized covariance matrix.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' pmat <- matrix(c(0.5, 0.2, 0.5, 0.2), nrow = 2)\n#' covmat <- cov(t(pmat))\n#' standard_cov_by_het(pmat, covmat)\nstandard_cov_by_het <- function(pmat, covmat) {\n  stopifnot(ncol(pmat) == ncol(covmat))\n  half_het_sums <- 0.5 * apply(pmat, MARGIN = 2, FUN = sum_of_het)\n  stopifnot(all(half_het_sums > 0))\n  # standaridize variances\n  diag(covmat) <- diag(covmat) / half_het_sums\n  # standardize covariances\n  for (i in 1:nrow(covmat)) {\n    for (j in 1:ncol(covmat)) {\n      if (i != j) {\n        covmat[i, j] <- covmat[i, j] / half_het_sums[min(c(i, j))]\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  return(covmat)\n}\n\n#' Calculate covariances from allele frequency matrix\n#'\n#' Computes the covariance matrix of allele frequency changes between\n#' adjacent generations (columns = time intervals), optionally with a sample\n#' size correction, heterozygosity standardization, arcsine-transformed\n#' input, and sign randomization for null comparisons.\n#'\n#' @param pmat Numeric matrix of allele frequencies; the first column is the\n#'   initial generation and time points ascend left to right.\n#' @param n Optional numeric vector of sample sizes (number of chromosomes\n#'   sampled per time point); required if `correct_for_n = TRUE`. Must have\n#'   one entry per time point (i.e., `ncol(pmat)`).\n#' @param correct_for_n Boolean; whether to correct covariances and variances\n#'   for finite sample size.\n#' @param standard_by_het Boolean; whether to standardize the covariance\n#'   matrix by heterozygosity via [standard_cov_by_het()].\n#' @param input_asin_trans Boolean; whether `pmat` holds arcsine-square-root\n#'   transformed frequencies (changes the sample size correction formulas).\n#' @param procedure Sign randomization procedure passed to\n#'   [sign_permute_increments()]; use `\"none\"` (default) for no\n#'   randomization.\n#' @param windows Optional vector of window IDs, one per row of `pmat`,\n#'   passed to [sign_permute_increments()] when `procedure = \"window\"`.\n#'\n#' @return The (optionally corrected/standardized) covariance matrix of\n#'   allele frequency changes.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' set.seed(1)\n#' pmat <- matrix(runif(15), nrow = 5, ncol = 3)\n#' covmat_from_pmat(pmat)\ncovmat_from_pmat <- function(pmat, n = NULL, correct_for_n = TRUE,\n                             standard_by_het = FALSE, input_asin_trans = FALSE,\n                             procedure = \"none\", windows = NULL) {\n  # allele frequency changes between adjacent generations\n  pdiff <- freq_increments(pmat)\n  # randomly swap signs of allele frequency changes\n  pdiff <- sign_permute_increments(pdiff, procedure = procedure, windows = windows)\n  # ensure pdiff is a matrix even with a single increment (2-column pmat)\n  if (is.null(dim(pdiff))) {\n    pdiff <- matrix(pdiff, ncol = 1)\n  }\n  # covariance matrices\n  covmat <- stats::cov(pdiff, use = \"pairwise.complete.obs\")\n  # correct for sample size, if needed\n  if (correct_for_n) {\n    if (any(n < 2)) {\n      stop(\"All n must be >= 2\")\n    }\n    if (length(n) != (ncol(covmat) + 1)) {\n      stop(\"Should be a sample size for every time point.\")\n    }\n    ### ARCSIN SQRT TRANSFORMED FREQUENCIES ###\n    if (input_asin_trans) {\n      # check transformed data are actually input\n      if (all(pmat[, 1] < pi)) {\n        warning(\"Are you sure values are arcsin transformed?\")\n      }\n      # correct overlapping covariances\n      # seq_len() yields integer(0) when ncol(covmat) == 1, so this is skipped\n      for (i in seq_len(ncol(covmat) - 1)) {\n        corrected_cov <- covmat[i, i + 1] + (1 / n[i + 1])\n        covmat[i, i + 1] <- corrected_cov\n        covmat[i + 1, i] <- corrected_cov\n      }\n      # correct variances\n      for (i in seq_len(ncol(covmat))) {\n        corrected_var <- covmat[i, i] - (1 / n[i]) - (1 / n[i + 1])\n        if (corrected_var < 0) {\n          warning(\"Sample size correction makes variance negative. Setting variance to zero\")\n          covmat[i, i] <- 0\n        } else {\n          covmat[i, i] <- corrected_var\n        }\n      }\n      ### RAW FREQUENCIES ###\n    } else {\n      # correct overlapping covariances\n      # seq_len() yields integer(0) when ncol(covmat) == 1, so this is skipped\n      for (i in seq_len(ncol(covmat) - 1)) {\n        corrected_cov <- mean(pdiff[, i] * pdiff[, i + 1], na.rm = TRUE) +\n          mean(pmat[, i + 1] * (1 - pmat[, i + 1]) / (n[i + 1] - 1), na.rm = TRUE)\n        covmat[i, i + 1] <- corrected_cov\n        covmat[i + 1, i] <- corrected_cov\n      }\n      # correct variances\n      for (i in seq_len(ncol(covmat))) {\n        corrected_var <- mean((pdiff[, i])^2, na.rm = TRUE) -\n          mean(pmat[, i] * (1 - pmat[, i]) / (n[i] - 1), na.rm = TRUE) -\n          mean(pmat[, i + 1] * (1 - pmat[, i + 1]) / (n[i + 1] - 1), na.rm = TRUE)\n        if (corrected_var < 0 | is.na(corrected_var)) {\n          warning(\"Sample size correction makes variance negative. Setting variance to zero\")\n          covmat[i, i] <- 0\n        } else {\n          covmat[i, i] <- corrected_var\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (standard_by_het) {\n    covmat <- standard_cov_by_het(pmat[, -ncol(pmat), drop = FALSE], covmat)\n  }\n\n  return(covmat)\n}\n\n#' Rolling sum of matrix, starting from top left\n#'\n#' Sums the elements of nested top-left squares of a square matrix: element\n#' 1 is `mat[1, 1]`, element 2 is `sum(mat[1:2, 1:2])`, and so on up to the\n#' full matrix sum.\n#'\n#' @param mat A square numeric matrix.\n#'\n#' @return A numeric vector of length `ncol(mat)`: the sums of the nested\n#'   top-left squares.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' rolling_matrix_sum(matrix(1:9, nrow = 3))\nrolling_matrix_sum <- function(mat) {\n  stopifnot(nrow(mat) == ncol(mat))\n  rolling_sum <- c()\n  for (i in 1:ncol(mat)) {\n    rolling_sum <- c(rolling_sum, sum(mat[1:i, 1:i]))\n  }\n  stopifnot(length(rolling_sum) == ncol(mat))\n  return(rolling_sum)\n}\n\n#' G statistic, corrected for selection increasing variance in allele\n#' frequency change\n#'\n#' Computes G' (Buffalo and Coop style): 1 minus the expected drift-only\n#' variance `times * E[p0(1-p0)] / (2N)`, scaled by the observed rolling sums\n#' of the (optionally absolute-valued) temporal covariance matrix. Values\n#' near 1 indicate covariance consistent with linked selection; values near\n#' or below 0 indicate drift-like, uncorrelated change.\n#'\n#' @param times Numeric vector of time points, one per interval of `pmat`\n#'   (length `ncol(pmat) - 1`), used to order the rolling sums.\n#' @param pmat Numeric matrix of allele frequencies, rows = variants,\n#'   columns = time points ascending; the first column is the initial\n#'   generation.\n#' @param N Effective population size.\n#' @param n Numeric vector of sample sizes (chromosomes) per time point,\n#'   passed to [covmat_from_pmat()] for the sample size correction.\n#' @param take_abs Boolean; whether to accumulate the absolute values of the\n#'   covariance matrix instead of the raw values.\n#'\n#' @return A numeric vector, one entry per time point: the corrected G\n#'   statistic accumulated up to that time.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' set.seed(1)\n#' pmat <- matrix(runif(15), nrow = 5, ncol = 3)\n#' g_prime(times = 2:3, pmat = pmat, N = 100, n = c(50, 50, 50))\ng_prime <- function(times, pmat, N, n, take_abs = FALSE) {\n  stopifnot(all(times >= 0), N > 2)\n  covmat <- covmat_from_pmat(pmat, n)\n  ep0 <- mean(pmat[, 1] * (1 - pmat[, 1]), na.rm = TRUE)\n  if (take_abs) {\n    var_roll <- rolling_matrix_sum(abs(covmat))\n  } else {\n    var_roll <- rolling_matrix_sum(covmat)\n  }\n  stopifnot(length(times) == length(var_roll))\n  return(1 - (times * ep0) / (2 * N * var_roll))\n}\n\n#' Calculate linked selection ratios from covariance matrix\n#'\n#' Accumulates variances (diagonal) and covariances (strict upper triangle)\n#' of a temporal covariance matrix over nested top-left squares and derives\n#' several G-style ratios of shared to total variance in allele frequency\n#' change.\n#'\n#' @param covmat Square covariance matrix of allele frequency changes, one\n#'   row/column per time interval.\n#'\n#' @return A data.frame with one row per time point (`gen`) and columns for\n#'   the G ratios (`gt`, `gt_abs`, `gt_abs_2`, `gt_pos`), the accumulated\n#'   sums (`sum_cov`, `sum_abs_cov`, `sum_pos_cov`, `sum_neg_cov`,\n#'   `sum_var`), and the positive-covariance fraction (`ratio`).\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' covmat <- matrix(c(1, 0.5, 0.2, 0.5, 2, 0.3, 0.2, 0.3, 3), nrow = 3)\n#' gt_from_covmat(covmat)\ngt_from_covmat <- function(covmat) {\n  covmat[lower.tri(covmat)] <- NA\n\n  covariances <- covmat[upper.tri(covmat)]\n  variances <- diag(covmat)\n\n  sums_var <- cumsum(variances)\n\n  sums_cov <- c(0)\n  sums_abs_cov <- c(0)\n  sums_pos_cov <- c(0)\n  sums_neg_cov <- c(0)\n  for (j in 2:nrow(covmat)) {\n    cov_sub <- covariances[1:(((j - 1) * (j)) / 2)]\n\n    sum_abs_cov <- 2 * sum(abs(cov_sub), na.rm = TRUE)\n    sum_cov <- 2 * sum(cov_sub, na.rm = TRUE)\n    sum_neg_cov <- 2 * sum(abs(cov_sub[(cov_sub < 0)]), na.rm = TRUE)\n    sum_pos_cov <- 2 * sum(cov_sub[(cov_sub > 0)], na.rm = TRUE)\n\n    sums_cov <- c(sums_cov, sum_cov)\n    sums_abs_cov <- c(sums_abs_cov, sum_abs_cov)\n    sums_pos_cov <- c(sums_pos_cov, sum_pos_cov)\n    sums_neg_cov <- c(sums_neg_cov, sum_neg_cov)\n  }\n\n  result <- data.frame(\n    gen = 1:nrow(covmat),\n    gt = sums_cov / (sums_var + sums_cov),\n    gt_abs = sums_abs_cov / (sums_var + sums_abs_cov),\n    gt_abs_2 = sums_abs_cov / (sums_var + sums_cov),\n    gt_pos = sums_pos_cov / (sums_var + sums_pos_cov),\n    sum_cov = sums_cov,\n    sum_abs_cov = sums_abs_cov,\n    sum_pos_cov = sums_pos_cov,\n    sum_neg_cov = sums_neg_cov,\n    sum_var = sums_var,\n    ratio = sums_pos_cov / (sums_pos_cov + sums_neg_cov)\n  )\n  return(result)\n}\n\n#' Calculate convergence correlation within environment\n#'\n#' Estimates the correlation of allele frequency changes among independent\n#' replicate populations within the same environment: the mean off-diagonal\n#' covariance divided by the geometric mean of the replicate variances.\n#'\n#' @param pdiff Numeric matrix of allele frequency changes, rows = variants,\n#'   columns = replicate time series (all replicates of one site, one time\n#'   point), with at least 2 rows and 2 columns.\n#'\n#' @return A numeric vector of length 2: `c(numerator, denominator)` \u2014 the\n#'   mean between-replicate covariance and the geometric mean within-replicate\n#'   variance.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' set.seed(1)\n#' pdiff <- matrix(rnorm(40, sd = 0.05), nrow = 20, ncol = 2)\n#' conv_cor_wn_env(pdiff)\nconv_cor_wn_env <- function(pdiff) {\n  stopifnot(ncol(pdiff) > 1, nrow(pdiff) > 1)\n  covmat <- stats::cov(pdiff, use = \"pairwise.complete.obs\")\n  rep_var <- diag(covmat)\n  rep_cov <- covmat[upper.tri(covmat)]\n  numerator <- sum(2 * rep_cov, na.rm = TRUE) / (2 * length(rep_cov))\n  denominator <- geom_pairwise_mean(rep_var)\n  stopifnot(denominator > 0, abs(numerator) <= denominator)\n  return(c(numerator, denominator))\n}\n\n#' Replicate G(t): proportion of variance in allele frequency change due to\n#' shared selection pressure\n#'\n#' Splits the covariance matrix of allele frequency changes into\n#' within-replicate variances and between-replicate covariances using the\n#' supplied replicate and time labels, and returns means and totals of each\n#' (raw, positive-only, and absolute-valued), for estimating the fraction of\n#' variance in allele frequency change attributable to shared selection.\n#'\n#' @param pdiff Numeric matrix of allele frequency changes, rows = variants,\n#'   columns = replicate time series.\n#' @param rep_labels Vector of replicate labels, one per column of `pdiff`.\n#' @param time_labels Vector of time point labels, one per column of\n#'   `pdiff`; must include at least 2 distinct values, as must `rep_labels`.\n#'\n#' @return A one-row data.frame with mean and total (raw, positive, absolute,\n#'   and trace) within-replicate variances and between-replicate covariances,\n#'   plus the counts of replicates (`n_var`) and replicate pairs\n#'   (`n_covar`).\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' set.seed(1)\n#' pdiff <- matrix(rnorm(60, sd = 0.05), nrow = 15, ncol = 4)\n#' replicate_gt(pdiff, rep_labels = c(1, 1, 2, 2), time_labels = c(1, 2, 1, 2))\nreplicate_gt <- function(pdiff, rep_labels, time_labels) {\n  stopifnot(ncol(pdiff) > 1,\n            nrow(pdiff) > 1,\n            length(rep_labels) == ncol(pdiff),\n            length(time_labels) == ncol(pdiff),\n            length(unique(rep_labels)) >= 2,\n            length(unique(time_labels)) >= 2)\n\n  rep_eq_bool_mat <- outer(rep_labels, rep_labels, \"==\")\n\n  time_eq_bool_mat <- outer(time_labels, time_labels, \"==\")\n\n  covmat <- stats::cov(pdiff, use = \"pairwise.complete.obs\")\n\n  # total variance within replicates\n  var_only_mat <- covmat[rep_eq_bool_mat]\n  total_var <- sum(var_only_mat)\n  total_var_pos <- sum(var_only_mat[(var_only_mat > 0)])\n  total_var_abs <- sum(abs(var_only_mat))\n  var_trace <- covmat[(rep_eq_bool_mat & time_eq_bool_mat)]\n  total_var_trace <- sum(var_trace)\n  n_var <- length(unique(rep_labels))\n\n  # total covariance across different replicates AND time points\n  cov_only_mat <- covmat[(!rep_eq_bool_mat) & (!time_eq_bool_mat)]\n  total_covar <- sum(cov_only_mat)\n  total_covar_abs <- sum(abs(cov_only_mat))\n  total_covar_pos <- sum(cov_only_mat[(cov_only_mat > 0)])\n  n_covar <- (n_var^2 - n_var) / 2\n\n  mean_var <- total_var / n_var\n  mean_var_pos <- total_var_pos / n_var\n  mean_var_abs <- total_var_abs / n_var\n  mean_var_trace <- total_var_trace / n_var\n  mean_covar <- total_covar / n_covar\n  mean_covar_pos <- total_covar_pos / n_covar\n  mean_covar_abs <- total_covar_abs / n_covar\n\n  stopifnot(total_covar <= total_covar_pos,\n            mean_covar <= mean_covar_pos,\n            total_var_pos <= total_var_abs,\n            total_covar < sum(abs(covmat)),\n            total_var < sum(abs(covmat)),\n            total_covar <= total_covar_abs,\n            isTRUE(all.equal(sum(var_only_mat) + sum(covmat[!rep_eq_bool_mat]),\n                             sum(covmat))),\n            mean_var >= 0,\n            total_var >= 0,\n            total_var_trace >= 0,\n            mean_var_trace >= 0)\n\n  return(data.frame(\n    mean_var = mean_var,\n    mean_var_pos = mean_var_pos,\n    mean_var_abs = mean_var_abs,\n    mean_var_trace = mean_var_trace,\n    mean_covar = mean_covar,\n    mean_covar_pos = mean_covar_pos,\n    mean_covar_abs = mean_covar_abs,\n    total_var = total_var,\n    total_var_pos = total_var_pos,\n    total_var_abs = total_var_abs,\n    total_var_trace = total_var_trace,\n    total_covar = total_covar,\n    total_covar_pos = total_covar_pos,\n    total_covar_abs = total_covar_abs,\n    n_var = n_var,\n    n_covar = n_covar\n  ))\n}\n\n#' Calculate covariances across a pair of environments\n#'\n#' Computes the mean standardized covariance of allele frequency changes\n#' between two populations: the average covariance between the two sets of\n#' replicate time series, normalized by the mean pairwise product of\n#' within-population standard deviations.\n#'\n#' @param pmat1 Numeric matrix of allele frequencies in population 1, rows =\n#'   variants, columns = replicate time series. Column names must contain\n#'   `pop1`.\n#' @param pmat2 Numeric matrix of allele frequencies in population 2, same\n#'   layout as `pmat1`. Column names must contain `pop2`.\n#' @param pop1 Character string identifying population 1; used to grep the\n#'   columns of `pmat1`.\n#' @param pop2 Character string identifying population 2; used to grep the\n#'   columns of `pmat2`.\n#' @param gen0 Numeric vector of allele frequencies at generation 0, one per\n#'   variant (shared by both populations).\n#'\n#' @return A single number: the mean standardized between-population\n#'   covariance.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' gen0 <- c(0.5, 0.4, 0.3)\n#' p1 <- cbind(rep_1 = gen0 + 0.01, rep_2 = gen0 - 0.01)\n#' p2 <- cbind(rep_1 = gen0 - 0.01, rep_2 = gen0 + 0.01)\n#' covmat_pop_pair(p1, p2, pop1 = \"rep\", pop2 = \"rep\", gen0 = gen0)\ncovmat_pop_pair <- function(pmat1, pmat2, pop1, pop2, gen0) {\n  stopifnot(\n    !is.null(colnames(pmat1)),\n    !is.null(colnames(pmat2))\n  )\n  # allele frequency changes between adjacent generations\n  pdiff1 <- pmat1 - gen0\n  pdiff2 <- pmat2 - gen0\n\n  covmat <- stats::cov(cbind(pdiff1, pdiff2), use = \"pairwise.complete.obs\")\n\n  # mean product of std of between population pairs\n  rep_var <- diag(covmat)\n  rep_var_1 <- rep_var[1:ncol(pmat1)]\n  rep_var_2 <- rep_var[(ncol(pmat1) + 1):length(rep_var)]\n  mean_pair_std <- mean(sqrt(rep_var_1 %o% rep_var_2))\n\n  bw_pop_cov <- covmat[base::grep(pop1, rownames(covmat)),\n                       base::grep(pop2, colnames(covmat))]\n\n  return(mean(bw_pop_cov) / mean_pair_std)\n}",
  "oldString": "  attr(out, \"sample_info\") <- sub_meta\n  class(out) <- c(\"freq_matrix\", class(out))\n  out\n}"
}

test_that("hill_weir_r2 matches the closed form at d = 0 and decays with distance", {
  # at d = 0, r2 = 5/11 * (1 + 36/(22n)), independent of C
  n <- 30
  expect_equal(
    hill_weir_r2(d = 0, n = n, C = 0.001),
    (10 / 22) * (1 + 36 / (n * 22))
  )
  expect_equal(
    hill_weir_r2(d = 0, n = n, C = 5),
    hill_weir_r2(d = 0, n = n, C = 0.001)
  )

  # LD decays with distance, and the function is vectorized in d
  r2 <- hill_weir_r2(d = c(0, 1000, 10000), n = n, C = 0.001)
  expect_length(r2, 3)
  expect_true(all(diff(r2) < 0))
})

2])\n  expect_equal(res[2], geom_pairwise_mean(diag(covmat)))\n  expect_lte(abs(res[1]), res[2])\n})\n\ntest_that(\"conv_cor_wn_env errors when replicates have zero variance\", {\n expect_error(g_prime(times = 2:3, pmat = pmat, N = 1, n = n), \"N > 2\")\n})\n\ntest_that(\"covmat_pop_pair computes mean standardized between-pop covariance\", {\n  set.seed(1)\n  L <- 10\n  gen0 <- runif(L, 0.3, 0.7)\n  p1 <- cbind(AA_R1 = gen0 + rnorm(L, 0, 0.02), AA_R2 = gen0 + rnorm(L, 0, 0.02))\n  p2 <- cbind(BB_R1 = gen0 + rnorm(L, 0, 0.02), BB_R2 = gen0 + rnorm(L, 0, 0.02))\n  val <- covmat_pop_pair(p1, p2, pop1 = \"AA\", pop2 = \"BB\", gen0 = gen0)\n\n  pd1 <- p1 - gen0\n  pd2 <- p2 - gen0\n  cm <- stats::cov(cbind(pd1, pd2))\n  rv1 <- diag(cm)[1:2]\n  rv2 <- diag(cm)[3:4]\n  mean_std <- mean(sqrt(rv1 %o% rv2))\n  bw <- mean(cm[1:2, 3:4])\n  expect_equal(val, bw / mean_std)\n})\n\ntest_that(\"covmat_pop_pair requires column names\", {\n  gen0 <- c(0.5, 0.4)\n  p1 <- _Thinking:_

Confirmed. `utils::head()` on a subclassed data.frame preserves the subclass, so `print(head(x))` re-dispatches to `print.snp_coords` → infinite recursion → C stack overflow. Matrix subclass print dispatch: print(head(round(fm,4))) — head.data.frame doesn't apply; for matrix class, head.default returns matrix with class preserved... Actually it passed, maybe because head.matrix drops... no, `head.matrix` also preserves attributes. Hmm, but the test passed for freq_mat and p0_vec. For p0_vec: class c("p0_vec","numeric"); head.default preserves class → print re-dispatches to print.p0_vec → recursion → but it PASSED. Odd — maybe head.default on a classed numeric doesn't preserve class in R 4.5? For freq_matrix it passed too. Whatever the difference (data.frame method chain vs atomic), the data.frame-based print methods clearly recurse. Fix: inside print methods, strip the subclass before printing. Standard approach: `print(NextMethod())` or use `utils:::print.data.frame` / `print.matrix` directly. Simplest: call `utils::head.data.frame`? That's internal-ish but exported? Not exported. Better: strip class: `print(utils::head(unclass(x)))` — for data.frames, unclass returns plain data.frame, head keeps plain, print dispatches print.data.frame. Same for matrix/vector.

{
    stopifnot(ncol(pdiff) >= 1, nrow(pdiff) >= 1)
    pdiff <- as.data.frame(pdiff)
    if (procedure == "window") {
        stopifnot(!is.null(windows), length(windows) == nrow(pdiff))
        pdiff$window <- windows
        pdiff <- dplyr::group_by(pdiff, window)
        pdiff <- dplyr::mutate(pdiff, dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), 
            ~.x * sample(c(1, -1), size = 1)))
        pdiff <- dplyr::ungroup(pdiff)
        pdiff <- pdiff[, setdiff(names(pdiff), "window"), drop = FALSE]
    }
    else if (procedure == "cell") {
        pdiff <- dplyr::mutate(pdiff, dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), 
            ~.x * sample(c(1, -1), dplyr::n(), replace = TRUE)))
    }
    else if (procedure == "genome") {
        sign_permutations <- sample(c(-1, 1), size = ncol(pdiff), 
            replace = TRUE)
        P <- diag(sign_permutations)
        pdiff <- as.matrix(pdiff) %*% P
    }
    else if (procedure == "none") {
    }
    else {
        stop("Procedure not valid. Choose from: none, window, cell, genome.")
    }
    return(pdiff)
}

## Assistant (Build · GLM-5.3-Flash · 21.8s)

_Thinking:_

The genome match works when the RNG order is: create matrix (consumes runif(20)), set.seed(7), draw sm... wait no. In my last test: `set.seed(7)`, create mat, then `sm <- sample(...)` — so sm is the SECOND draw after seed 7. Then re-seed, create mat2, call fn. Both do: seed → runif(20) → sample(4). That matches!

Earlier confusion: my colSums-based sign inference was unreliable (colSums near zero). And my first test drew `sm` without re-creating the matrix in between.

So the function IS deterministic. The genome test needs: seed → mat → reseed → mat2 → sm → compare. Actually simpler: in the test, create the matrix, then set.seed(7), then draw sm, then set.seed(7) again?? No wait.

Test currently does:
```r
set.seed(7)
mat <- as.data.frame(matrix(runif(20, ...), 5, 4))
signs <- c(1, -1, -1, 1)  # unused now
P <- diag(signs)
expected <- as.matrix(mat) %*% P
set.seed(7)
flipped <- sample(c(-1, 1), size = 4, replace = TRUE)
expected <- as.matrix(mat) %*% diag(flipped)
result_genome <- sign_permute_increments(mat, procedure = "genome")
```
Here: set.seed(7) → runif(20) → [reseed] → sample → that's draw #1 after seed. The function call then does: (no RNG before sample) sample → but wait, the function saw RNG state AFTER the sample(flipped) call. So the function's draw is the SECOND sample after seed 7. Fix: re-seed before drawing flipped AND recreate nothing — the function must see the same state: `set.seed(7); flipped <- sample(...)` then `set.seed(7); flipped2...` no.

Correct order in test:
```r
set.seed(7)
mat <- as.data.frame(matrix(runif(20), 5, 4))
set.seed(7)
flipped <- sample(c(-1, 1), size = 4, replace = TRUE)
expected <- as.matrix(mat) %*% diag(flipped)
set.seed(7)
result_genome <- sign_permute_increments(mat, procedure = "genome")  # draws sample as first RNG use after seed
```
That's it: reseed right before the function call (function's sample is its first RNG consumption — as.data.frame consumes nothing). Earlier manual repro confirmed: inline `pdiff <- as.data.frame(mat); sample(...)` after set.seed gives 1 -1 -1 1 and... wait but earlier "inline vs fn: FALSE". Because in that repro I created mat with runif AFTER set.seed, then called inline path (sample draw) and then called fn — fn saw RNG state after the inline draw. The order was wrong in that comparison, not the function.

OK so test fix: 
```r
set.seed(7)
mat <- as.data.frame(...)
set.seed(7)
flipped <- sample(c(-1,1), 4, replace = TRUE)
expected <- as.matrix(mat) %*% diag(flipped)
set.seed(7)
result <- sign_permute_increments(mat, procedure = "genome")
expect_equal(as.matrix(result), expected)
```

Window test fix: signs are per (window, column) — constant within window rows for each column. My test asserted all columns share a sign within a window. Fix: for each window w and column j: all(signs[idx, j] == signs[idx[1], j]).

Also 122: unname() doesn't strip class. Use `expect_identical(unclass(fm), unname(m))`? unclass(fm) still has class attr removed... freq_matrix class vector is c("freq_matrix", "matrix", "array"); unclass removes the class attribute entirely → plain matrix. But m has dimnames? Both unnamed. So `expect_identical(unclass(fm), m)`.

But wait — `expect_identical(unclass(fm), unname(m))`: fm = m exactly (same dimnames = NULL). unclass(fm) removes class attr. unname(m) strips dimnames (already NULL). Should pass. Actually cleaner: `expect_identical(unclass(fm), m)`.

488: rolling_matrix_sum(matrix(1:6, nrow=3)) — 1:6 with 3 rows = 3x2, NOT square! Need 9 elements: matrix(1:9, nrow=3).

545 warning: rnorm(20) with nrow=5, ncol=2 recycles (20=5*2 ✓ length OK but "data length differs from size of matrix: 20 != 5 x 2"? 5*2=10 ≠ 20!). matrix(rnorm(20), nrow=5, ncol=2) → data has 20 elements, matrix 5x2=10. Need ncol=4 for 20 elements (5x4). pdiff with 4 columns: rep_labels must be length 4. Fix: use matrix(rnorm(20), nrow=5, ncol=4), rep_labels=c(1,2), time_labels=c(1,2).

Root cause found for the "non-determinism": it was my test's RNG order (the function's `sample()` must be the *first* draw after `set.seed(7)`) plus an unreliable `colSums`-based sign inference. The function is fine. Fixing the remaining test bugs:

test_that("sign_permute_increments genome mode flips whole columns", {
  set.seed(7)
  mat <- as.data.frame(matrix(runif(20, min = -1, max = 1), nrow = 5, ncol = 4))
  result_genome <- sign_permute_increments(mat, procedure = "genome")

  # each result column is a single +1/-1 multiple of the corresponding input column
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(mat))) {
    col_signs <- as.matrix(result_genome)[, j] / as.matrix(mat)[, j]
    expect_true(all(col_signs == col_signs[1]))
    expect_true(all(abs(col_signs) == 1))
  }

  # reproducible: same seed, same result
  set.seed(7)
  result_again <- sign_permute_increments(mat, procedure = "genome")
  expect_equal(as.matrix(result_again), as.matrix(result_genome))
})

The error is thrown but `expect_error(..., "nrow(mat) == ncol(mat)")` treats it as ERROR not success? The message "nrow(mat) == ncol(mat) is not TRUE" should match the regex "nrow(mat) == ncol(mat)". ## Plan — README overhaul (exhaustive listing + table of contents)

All 37 exports from NAMESPACE accounted for, grouped to mirror the package's module structure (`plotting.R`, `statistics.R`, `popgen.R`, `file_management.R`). The 4 `print.*` S3 methods stay unlisted (documented with their constructors, per convention).

**Structure:**

```markdown
# rventures

An R package of convenience functions for use across RStudio projects.

## Contents

- [Installation](#installation)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [Functions](#functions)
  - [Plotting](#plotting)
  - [Statistics](#statistics)
  - [Population genetics](#population-genetics)
  - [Temporal-replicate toolkit](#temporal-replicate-toolkit)
  - [Dataset structures](#dataset-structures)
  - [File management](#file-management)
- [Development](#development)

## Installation        <- unchanged (lines 5-17)

## Usage               <- unchanged (lines 19-23)

## Functions

### Plotting
- `save_plot()` — save a ggplot as PDF/PNG with by-date/by-analysis symlinks
- `plot_groups_pdf()` — split a data frame by grouping columns and write one plot per group to a multi-page PDF
- `plot_manhattan()` — GWAS Manhattan plot with per-chromosome x-axis and optional SNP highlighting
- `plot_paf_dotplot()` — dotplot of aligned feature (PAF) coordinates, query vs. target
- `plot_var_cov_matrix()` — upper-triangle heatmap of a variance-covariance matrix
- `plot_predictions_truth_scatter()` — predictions vs. truth scatter with identity line, fit, and correlation stats

### Statistics
- `corr_ci_autocorr()` — Pearson correlation CI adjusted for AR(1) autocorrelation
- `lm_sim()`, `multicol_sim()` — linear-model simulations

### Population genetics
- `fitfreq()`, `WF_sel()` — selection/drift allele-frequency simulations
- `fc()` — standardized variance in allele-frequency change (Waples 1989)
- `waples_ne()` — temporal Ne estimate corrected for selfing
- `hill_weir_r2()` — expected LD (r^2) between loci a given distance apart (Hill & Weir 1988)

### Temporal-replicate toolkit
- `freq_increments()` — allele-frequency changes between adjacent time points
- `rm_na_after_na()` — NA-truncate a time series at its first NA
- `arcsin_sqrt()` — variance-stabilizing arcsine-square-root transform
- `sum_of_het()`, `geom_pairwise_mean()`, `rolling_matrix_sum()` — small matrix/vector helpers
- `sign_permute_increments()` — sign randomization (window/cell/genome) for null tests
- `covmat_from_pmat()` — covariance matrix of allele-frequency changes, with sample-size correction and heterozygosity standardization
- `standard_cov_by_het()` — standardize a covariance matrix by heterozygosity
- `g_prime()` — linked-selection G statistic corrected for selection-inflated variance
- `gt_from_covmat()` — G ratios accumulated over nested top-left squares of a covariance matrix
- `conv_cor_wn_env()` — convergence correlation among replicates within an environment
- `replicate_gt()` — variance/covariance partition by replicate and time labels
- `covmat_pop_pair()` — mean standardized covariance between a pair of populations

### Dataset structures
- `freq_matrix()` — validated L x S allele-frequency matrix
- `snp_coords()` — validated L x 2 chromosome/position table
- `p0_vec()` — validated initial allele-frequency vector
- `sample_info()` — validated S x 3 population/time/replicate metadata
- `validate_af_dataset()` — cross-check the four objects for consistent dimensions
- `extract_samples()` — subset a freq_matrix by population/time/replicate with rebuilt column names

### File management
- `read_paf()` — read a PAF alignment file
- `append_table()` — append a data frame to a file
- `check_file_exists()` — stop with an informative error if a file is missing

## User
I have this function that uses the rabc package. The user of my r package probably won't need this function very often, so is there a way to include the function in the package, but avoid installing rabc unless it's necessary? Also, I tried to suppress warnings and messages for the package, but it never really worked. The function would still print a small summary of abc results with each call. Can you take a crack at that problem too? # evaluate abc model similar to cnn (performance on validation data after training on training data)
# use training data to make a prediction about a validation data point
# repeat for all validation data points
train_abc = function(train_sample, val_sample, outcomes, summary_stats, tol, method){
  # vectors to store results
  lwr_results = c()
  median_results = c()
  mean_results = c()
  mode_results = c()
  upr_results = c()
  
  # subset frames to relevant metrics
  train_outcomes = train_sample[,outcomes]
  train_stats = train_sample[,summary_stats]
  val_stats = val_sample[,summary_stats]
  
  # loop over validation data
  for(i in 1:nrow(val_stats)){
    print(paste("Validation example: ", i, sep = ""))
    
    # get one validation simulation
    val_target = val_stats[i,]
    
    # run abc on validation sim
    result = suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(abc(val_target, train_outcomes, train_stats, tol, method)))
    #msgs <- invisible(suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(capture.output(capture.output(result <- abc(val_target, train_outcomes, train_stats, tol, method), type = "message"), type="output"))))
    
    #cred_int = round(quantile(my_prediction$unadj.values, c(0.055, 0.945)))
    result_summary = suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(summary(result)))
    cred_int = round(c(result_summary[[2]], result_summary[[6]]))
    median_est = round(result_summary[[3]])
    mean_est = round(result_summary[[4]])
    mode_est = round(result_summary[[5]])
    
    # save prediction
    lwr_results = c(lwr_results, cred_int[1])
    median_results = c(median_results, median_est)
    mean_results = c(mean_results, mean_est)
    mode_results = c(mode_results, mode_est)
    upr_results = c(upr_results, cred_int[2])
  }
  
  return(
    data.frame(
      truth = val_sample[,outcomes],
      lwr_cred_int = lwr_results,
      pred_mean = mean_results,
      pred_median = median_results,
      pred_mode = mode_results,
      upr_cred_int = upr_results
    )
  )

######################################################################

abc <- function(target, param, sumstat, tol, method, hcorr = TRUE,
                transf = "none", logit.bounds = c(0,0), subset = NULL,
                kernel = "epanechnikov", numnet = 10, sizenet = 5,
                lambda = c(0.0001,0.001,0.01), trace = FALSE, maxit =
                500, ...){
    
    call <- match.call()
    
    ## general checks that the function is used correctly
    ## ###################################################
    
    if(missing(target)) stop("'target' is missing")
    if(missing(param)) stop("'param' is missing")
    if(missing(sumstat)) stop("'sumstat' is missing")
    if(!is.matrix(param) && !is.data.frame(param) && !is.vector(param)) stop("'param' has to be a matrix, data.frame or vector.")
    if(!is.matrix(sumstat) && !is.data.frame(sumstat) && !is.vector(sumstat)) stop("'sumstat' has to be a matrix, data.frame or vector.")
    if(missing(tol)) stop("'tol' is missing")
    if(missing(method)) stop("'method' is missing with no default")  
    if(!any(method == c("rejection", "loclinear", "neuralnet","ridge"))){
        stop("Method must be rejection, loclinear, or neuralnet or ridge")
    }
    if(method == "rejection") rejmethod <- TRUE
    else rejmethod <- FALSE
    
    if(!any(kernel == c("gaussian", "epanechnikov", "rectangular", "triangular", "biweight", "cosine"))){
        kernel <- "epanechnikov"
        warning("Kernel is incorrectly defined. Setting to default (Epanechnikov)")
    }

    if(is.data.frame(param)) param <- as.matrix(param)
    if(is.data.frame(sumstat)) sumstat <- as.matrix(sumstat)
    if(is.list(target)) target <- unlist(target)
    if(is.vector(sumstat)) sumstat <- matrix(sumstat, ncol=1)
    if(length(target)!=dim(sumstat)[2]) stop("Number of summary statistics in 'target' has to be the same as in 'sumstat'.")
    
    ## stop if zero var in sumstat
    ## #########################
    nss <- length(sumstat[1,])
    cond1 <- !any(as.logical(apply(sumstat, 2, function(x) length(unique(x))-1)))
    if(cond1) stop("Zero variance in the summary statistics.")
    
    
    ## transformations
    ## ################
    ltransf <- length(transf)
    if(is.vector(param)){
        numparam <- 1
        param <- matrix(param, ncol=1)
    }
    else numparam <- dim(param)[2]
    for (i in 1:ltransf){
        if(sum(transf[i] == c("none","log","logit")) == 0){
            stop("Transformations must be none, log, or logit.")
        }
        if(transf[i]=="logit"){
            if(logit.bounds[i,1] >= logit.bounds[i,2]){
                stop("Logit bounds are incorrect.")       
            }
        }
    }
    ## if no logit change logit.bounds to NULL
    ## if(any(transf) == "logit") logit.bounds <- NULL
    
    ## no transformation should be applied when rejmethod is true
    if(rejmethod){
        if(!all(transf == "none")){
            warning("No transformation is applied when the simple rejection is used.", call.=F)
        }
        transf[1:numparam] <- "none"
    }
    else{
        if(numparam != ltransf){
            if(length(transf) == 1){
                transf <- rep(transf[1], numparam)
                warning("All parameters are \"", transf[1], "\" transformed.", sep="", call.=F)
            }
            else stop("Number of parameters is not the same as number of transformations.", sep="", call.=F)
        }
    }
    
    ## parameter and/or sumstat values that are to be excluded
    ## #######################################################
    gwt <- rep(TRUE,length(sumstat[,1]))
    gwt[attributes(na.omit(sumstat))$na.action] <- FALSE
    if(missing(subset)) subset <- rep(TRUE,length(sumstat[,1]))
    gwt <- as.logical(gwt*subset)
    
    ## extract names of parameters and statistics if given
    ## ###################################################
    if(!length(colnames(param))){
        warning("No parameter names are given, using P1, P2, ...")
        paramnames <- paste("P", 1:numparam, sep="")
    }
    else paramnames <- colnames(param)
    
    if(!length(colnames(sumstat))){
        warning("No summary statistics names are given, using S1, S2, ...")
        statnames <- paste("S", 1:nss, sep="")
    }
    else statnames <- colnames(sumstat)
    
    ## scale everything
    ## #################
    
    scaled.sumstat <- sumstat
    for(j in 1:nss){
        scaled.sumstat[,j] <- normalise(sumstat[,j],sumstat[,j][gwt])
    }
    
    for(j in 1:nss){
        target[j] <- normalise(target[j],sumstat[,j][gwt])
    }
    
    ## calculate euclidean distance
    ## ############################
    sum1 <- 0
    for(j in 1:nss){
        sum1 <- sum1 + (scaled.sumstat[,j]-target[j])^2
    }
    dist <- sqrt(sum1)
    
    ## includes the effect of gwt in the tolerance
    dist[!gwt] <- floor(max(dist[gwt])+10)
    
    ## wt1 defines the region we're interested in

    ceiling(length(dist)*tol)->nacc
    sort(dist)[nacc]->ds
    wt1 <- (dist <= ds)
    aux<-cumsum(wt1)
    wt1 <- wt1 & (aux<=nacc)
    if(kernel == "gaussian") 
    {
    	wt1 <- rep(TRUE, length(dist))
    }
    ## transform parameters
    ## ######################
    for (i in 1:numparam){
        if(transf[i] == "log"){
            if(min(param[,i]) <= 0){
                cat("log transform: values out of bounds - correcting...")
                x.tmp <- ifelse(param[,i] <= 0,max(param[,i]),param[,i])
                x.tmp.min <- min(x.tmp)
                param[,i] <- ifelse(param[,i] <= 0, x.tmp.min,param[,i])
            }
            param[,i] <- log(param[,i])
        }
        else if(transf[i] == "logit"){
            if(min(param[,i]) <= logit.bounds[i,1]){
                x.tmp <- ifelse(param[,i] <= logit.bounds[i,1],max(param[,i]),param[,i])
                x.tmp.min <- min(x.tmp)
                param[,i] <- ifelse(param[,i] <= logit.bounds[i,1], x.tmp.min,param[,i])
            }
            if(max(param[,i]) >= logit.bounds[i,2]){
                x.tmp <- ifelse(param[,i] >= logit.bounds[i,2],min(param[,i]),param[,i])
                x.tmp.max <- max(x.tmp)
                param[,i] <- ifelse(param[,i] >= logit.bounds[i,2], x.tmp.max,param[,i])
            }
            param[,i] <- (param[,i]-logit.bounds[i,1])/(logit.bounds[i,2]-logit.bounds[i,1])
            param[,i] <- log(param[,i]/(1-param[,i]))
        }
    } # end of parameter transformations
    
    ## select summary statistics in region
    ## ###################################
    ss <- sumstat[wt1,]
    unadj.values <- param[wt1,]
    
    ## if simple rejection or in the selected region there is no var in sumstat
    ## ########################################################################
    statvar <- as.logical(apply(cbind(sumstat[wt1,]), 2, function(x) length(unique(x))-1))
    cond2 <- !any(statvar)
    
    if(cond2 && !rejmethod)
        stop("Zero variance in the summary statistics in the selected region. Try: checking summary statistics, choosing larger tolerance, or rejection method.")
    
    if(rejmethod){
        if(cond2) warning("Zero variance in the summary statistics in the selected region. Check summary statistics, consider larger tolerance.")
        weights <- rep(1,length=sum(wt1))
        adj.values <- NULL
        residuals <- NULL
        lambda <- NULL
    }
    
    else{
        if(cond2) cat("Warning messages:\nStatistic(s)", statnames[!statvar], "has/have zero variance in the selected region.\nConsider using larger tolerance or the rejection method or discard this/these statistics, which might solve the collinearity problem in 'lsfit'.\n", sep=", ")
        
        ## weights
        if(kernel == "epanechnikov") weights <- 1 - (dist[wt1]/ds)^2
        if(kernel == "rectangular") weights <- dist[wt1]/ds
        if(kernel == "gaussian") weights <- 1/sqrt(2*pi)*exp(-0.5*(dist/(ds/2))^2)
        if(kernel == "triangular") weights <- 1 - abs(dist[wt1]/ds)
        if(kernel == "biweight") weights <- (1 - (dist[wt1]/ds)^2)^2
        if(kernel == "cosine") weights <- cos(pi/2*dist[wt1]/ds)
        
        ## regression correction
        ## ######################
        if(method == "loclinear"){
            
           fit1 <- lsfit(scaled.sumstat[wt1,],param[wt1,],wt=weights)
            #pred <- t(fit1$coeff) %*% c(1,target)
            pred <- t(structure(cbind(fit1$coefficients)[fit1$qr$pivot,], names=names(fit1$coefficients))) %*% c(1,target)
            
            pred <- matrix(pred, ncol=numparam, nrow=sum(wt1), byrow=TRUE)
            #residuals <- fit1$residuals
            residuals<-param[wt1,]-t(t(structure(cbind(fit1$coefficients)[fit1$qr$pivot,], names=names(fit1$coefficients))) %*%t(cbind(1,scaled.sumstat[wt1,])))
	    	residuals<-cbind(residuals)
	    	#rrr<<-residuals
	    	the_m<-apply(residuals,FUN=mean,2)
	    	residuals<-sapply(1:numparam,FUN=function(x){residuals[,x]-the_m[x]})
	    	pred <- sapply(1:numparam,FUN=function(x){pred[,x]+the_m[x]})

            
            sigma2<-apply(as.matrix(residuals),FUN=function(x){sum((x)^2 *weights)/sum(weights)},MARGIN=2)	
            aic<-sum(wt1)*sum(log(sigma2))+2*(nss+1)*numparam
            bic<-sum(wt1)*sum(log(sigma2))+log(sum(wt1))*(nss+1)*numparam
            
            if(hcorr == TRUE){
                 fit2 <- lsfit(scaled.sumstat[wt1,],log(residuals^2),wt=weights)
                auxaux<-t(structure(cbind(fit2$coefficients)[fit2$qr$pivot,], names=names(fit2$coefficients))) %*% c(1,target)
                pred.sd <- sqrt(exp(auxaux))
                pred.sd <- matrix(pred.sd, nrow=sum(wt1), ncol=numparam, byrow=T)
                pred.si<-t(t(structure(cbind(fit2$coefficients)[fit2$qr$pivot,], names=names(fit2$coefficients))) %*%t(cbind(1,scaled.sumstat[wt1,])))
                pred.si<-sqrt(exp(pred.si))
               	#residuals2<-log(residuals^2)-t(t(structure(cbind(fit2$coefficients)[fit2$qr$pivot,], names=names(fit2$coefficients))) %*%t(cbind(1,scaled.sumstat[wt1,])))
                #fv <- sqrt(exp(log(fit1$residuals^2) - fit2$residuals))
                #fv <- sqrt(exp(residuals2))
               # adj.values <- pred + (pred.sd*residuals) / fv # correction heteroscedasticity
               adj.values <- pred + (pred.sd*residuals) / pred.si
               residuals<-(pred.sd*residuals) / pred.si
            }
            else{
                adj.values <- pred + residuals
            }
            colnames(adj.values) <- colnames(unadj.values)
            lambda <- NULL
        }
        
        ## neural network regression
        ## ##########################
        if(method == "neuralnet"){
            linout <- TRUE
            
            ## normalise parameters
            param.mad <- c()
            for(i in 1:numparam){
                param.mad[i] <- mad(param[,i][gwt]) # save for renormalisation
                param[,i] <- normalise(param[,i],param[,i][gwt])
            }
            
            lambda <- sample(lambda, numnet, replace=T)
            fv <- array(dim=c(sum(wt1), numparam, numnet))
            pred <- matrix(nrow=numparam, ncol=numnet)
            for (i in 1:numnet){
                fit1 <- nnet(scaled.sumstat[wt1,], param[wt1,], weights = weights, decay = lambda[i],
                             size = sizenet, trace = trace, linout = linout, maxit = maxit, ...)
                cat(i)
                fv[,,i] <- fit1$fitted.values
                pred[,i] <- predict(fit1, data.frame(rbind(target)))
            }
            cat("\n")
            pred.med <- apply(pred, 1, median)
            pred.med <- matrix(pred.med, nrow=sum(wt1), ncol=numparam, byrow=T)
            fitted.values <- apply(fv, c(1,2), median)
            residuals <- param[wt1,] - fitted.values # median of fitted values par nnets for each accepted point and parameter
            
            if(hcorr == TRUE){
                pred2 <- matrix(nrow=numparam, ncol=numnet)
                fv2 <- array(dim=c(sum(wt1), numparam, numnet))
                for (i in 1:numnet){
                    fit2 <- nnet(scaled.sumstat[wt1,], log(residuals^2), weights = weights, decay = lambda[i], size = sizenet, trace = trace, linout = linout, ...)
                    cat(i)
                    fv2[,,i] <- fit2$fitted.values
                    pred2[,i] <- predict(fit2, data.frame(rbind(target)))
                }
                cat("\n")
                pred.sd <- sqrt(exp(apply(pred2, 1, median)))
                pred.sd <- matrix(pred.sd, nrow=sum(wt1), ncol=numparam, byrow=T)
                fv.sd <- sqrt(exp(apply(fv2, c(1,2), median)))
                adj.values <- pred.med + (pred.sd*residuals)/fv.sd # correction heteroscedasticity
           		residuals<-(pred.sd*residuals)/fv.sd
           }
            else{
                adj.values <- pred.med + residuals
            }
            colnames(adj.values) <- colnames(unadj.values)
            
            ## renormalise
            for(i in 1:numparam){
                ##       residuals[,i] <- residuals[,i]*param.mad[i] not much sense...
                adj.values[,i] <- adj.values[,i]*param.mad[i]
            }
            
        } # end of neuralnet
             if(method == "ridge"){
            #print("la")
            ## normalise parameters
            param.mad <- c()
            for(i in 1:numparam){
                param.mad[i] <- mad(param[,i][gwt]) # save for renormalisation
                param[,i] <- normalise(param[,i],param[,i][gwt])
            }
           # print("ici")
            numnet<-length(lambda)
           #lambda <- sample(lambda, numnet, replace=T)
            fv <- array(dim=c(sum(wt1), numparam, numnet))
            pred <- matrix(nrow=numparam, ncol=numnet)
            mataux<-sqrt(diag(weights))
            paramaux<-as.matrix(mataux%*%param[wt1,])
            
            #print(dim(paramaux))
            scaledaux<-mataux%*%scaled.sumstat[wt1,]
            #targetaux<-drop(mataux%*%target
            for(parcur in (1:numparam))
            {
            	#cat(parcur)
            	fit1<-lm.ridge(paramaux[,parcur]~scaledaux,lambda=lambda)
            	for (i in 1:numnet){
            #   fit1 <- nnet(scaled.sumstat[wt1,], param[wt1,], weights = weights, decay = lambda[i],
            #                 size = sizenet, trace = trace, linout = linout, maxit = maxit, ...)
            #    cat(i)
            	    fv[,parcur,i] <- drop(cbind(1,scaled.sumstat[wt1,])%*%(rbind(coef(fit1))[i,]))
                	pred[parcur,i] <- drop(c(1, target) %*%(rbind(coef(fit1))[i,]))
            					}
            }
           # cat("\n")
            pred.med <- apply(pred, 1, median)
            pred.med <- matrix(pred.med, nrow=sum(wt1), ncol=numparam, byrow=T)
            fitted.values <- apply(fv, c(1,2), median)
            residuals <- param[wt1,] - fitted.values # median of fitted values par nnets for each accepted point and parameter
            
            if(hcorr == TRUE){
                pred2 <- matrix(nrow=numparam, ncol=numnet)
                fv2 <- array(dim=c(sum(wt1), numparam, numnet))
                 for(parcur in (1:numparam))
            	{
            		lresidaux<-(mataux%*%(log(residuals[,parcur]^2)))
              		fit2<-lm.ridge(lresidaux~scaledaux,lambda=lambda)
                	for (i in 1:numnet){
                    	#cat(i)
                    	fv2[,parcur,i] <- drop(cbind(1,scaled.sumstat[wt1,])%*%(rbind(coef(fit2))[i,]))
						pred2[parcur,i] <- drop(c(1, target) %*%(rbind(coef(fit2))[i,]))         
									}
                }
                cat("\n")
                pred.sd <- sqrt(exp(apply(pred2, 1, median)))
                pred.sd <- matrix(pred.sd, nrow=sum(wt1), ncol=numparam, byrow=T)
                fv.sd <- sqrt(exp(apply(fv2, c(1,2), median)))
                adj.values <- pred.med + (pred.sd*residuals)/fv.sd # correction heteroscedasticity
            	residuals<- (pred.sd*residuals)/fv.sd
            }
            else{
                adj.values <- pred.med + residuals
            }
            colnames(adj.values) <- colnames(unadj.values)
            
            ## renormalise
            for(i in 1:numparam){
                ##       residuals[,i] <- residuals[,i]*param.mad[i] not much sense...
                adj.values[,i] <- adj.values[,i]*param.mad[i]
            }
            
        } # end of ridge
        
    } # end of else than rejmethod
    
    ## back transform parameter values
    ## ################################
    if(numparam == 1){
        unadj.values <- matrix(unadj.values, ncol=1)
        if(method!="rejection")
        {adj.values <- matrix(adj.values, ncol=1)
        residuals <- matrix(residuals, ncol=1)}
    }
    
    for (i in 1:numparam){
        if(transf[i] == "log"){
            unadj.values[,i] <- exp(unadj.values[,i])
            adj.values[,i] <- exp(adj.values[,i])
        }
        else if(transf[i] == "logit"){
            unadj.values[,i] <- exp(unadj.values[,i])/(1+exp(unadj.values[,i]))
            unadj.values[,i] <- unadj.values[,i]*(logit.bounds[i,2]-logit.bounds[i,1])+logit.bounds[i,1]
            adj.values[,i] <- exp(adj.values[,i])/(1+exp(adj.values[,i]))
            adj.values[,i] <- adj.values[,i]*(logit.bounds[i,2]-logit.bounds[i,1])+logit.bounds[i,1]
        }
    }
    
    abc.return(transf, logit.bounds, method, call, numparam, nss, paramnames, statnames,
               unadj.values, adj.values, ss, weights, residuals, dist, wt1, gwt, lambda, hcorr,aic,bic)
    
}


abc.return <- function(transf, logit.bounds, method, call, numparam, nss, paramnames, statnames,
                       unadj.values, adj.values, ss, weights, residuals, dist, wt1, gwt, lambda, hcorr,aic,bic){
    
    if(method == "rejection"){
        out <- list(unadj.values=unadj.values, ss=ss, dist=dist,
                    call=call, na.action=gwt, region=wt1, transf=transf, logit.bounds = logit.bounds,
                    method="rejection", numparam=numparam, numstat=nss, names=list(parameter.names=paramnames, statistics.names=statnames))
    }
    else if(method == "loclinear"){
        out <- list(adj.values=adj.values, unadj.values=unadj.values,
                    ss=ss, weights=weights, residuals=residuals, dist=dist,
                    call=call, na.action=gwt, region=wt1, transf=transf, logit.bounds = logit.bounds,
                    method="loclinear", hcorr = hcorr, numparam=numparam, numstat=nss,aic=aic,bic=bic,
                    names=list(parameter.names=paramnames, statistics.names=statnames))
    }
    else if(method == "ridge"){
        out <- list(adj.values=adj.values, unadj.values=unadj.values,
                    ss=ss, weights=weights, residuals=residuals, dist=dist,
                    call=call, na.action=gwt, region=wt1, transf=transf, logit.bounds = logit.bounds,
                    method="ridge", hcorr = hcorr, numparam=numparam, numstat=nss,
                    names=list(parameter.names=paramnames, statistics.names=statnames))
    }
    else if(method == "neuralnet"){
        out <- list(adj.values=adj.values, unadj.values=unadj.values,
                    ss=ss, weights=weights, residuals=residuals, dist=dist,
                    call=call, na.action=gwt, region=wt1, transf=transf, logit.bounds = logit.bounds,
                    method="neuralnet", hcorr = hcorr, lambda=lambda, numparam=numparam, numstat=nss,
                    names=list(parameter.names=paramnames, statistics.names=statnames))
    }
    
    class(out) <- "abc"
    out
    
}

is.abc <- function(x){
    if (inherits(x, "abc")) TRUE
    else FALSE    
}

print.abc <- function(x, ...){
    if (!inherits(x, "abc")) 
        stop("Use only with objects of class \"abc\".", call.=F)
    abc.out <- x
    cl <- abc.out$call
    cat("Call:\n")
    dput(cl, control=NULL)
    
    cat("Method:\n")
    ## rejection
    if (abc.out$method == "rejection")
        cat("Rejection\n\n")
    ## loclinear
    else if (abc.out$method == "loclinear"){
        if(abc.out$hcorr == T){
            cat("Local linear regression\n")
            cat("with correction for heteroscedasticity\n\n")
        }
        else cat("Local linear regression\n\n")
    }
    ## ridge
    else if (abc.out$method == "ridge"){
        if(abc.out$hcorr == T){
            cat("Ridge regression\n")
            cat("with correction for heteroscedasticity\n\n")
        }
        else cat("Ridge regression\n\n")
    }
    ## nnet
    else if (abc.out$method == "neuralnet"){
        if(abc.out$hcorr == T){
            cat("Non-linear regression via neural networks\n")
            cat("with correction for heteroscedasticity\n\n")
        }
        else cat("Non-linear regression via neural networks\n\n")
    }
    cat("Parameters:\n")
    cat(abc.out$names$parameter.names, sep=", ")
    cat("\n\n")
    cat("Statistics:\n")
    cat(abc.out$names$statistics.names, sep=", ")
    cat("\n\n")        
    cat("Total number of simulations", length(abc.out$na.action), "\n\n")
    cat("Number of accepted simulations: ", dim(abc.out$unadj.values)[1], "\n\n")
    invisible(abc.out)
}

summary.abc <- function(object, unadj = FALSE, intvl = .95, print = TRUE, digits = max(3, getOption("digits")-3), ...){
  
  if (!inherits(object, "abc")) 
    stop("Use only with objects of class \"abc\".", call.=F)
  abc.out <- object
  np <- abc.out$numparam
  cl <- abc.out$call
  parnames <- abc.out$names[[1]]
  npri <- dim(abc.out$unadj.values)[1]
  npost <- dim(abc.out$unadj.values)[1]
  myprobs <- c((1-intvl)/2, 0.5, 1-(1-intvl)/2)
  
  if(print){
    cat("Call: \n")
    dput(cl, control=NULL)
  }
  
  if(abc.out$method == "rejection" || unadj){
    if(print) cat(paste("Data:\n abc.out$unadj.values (",npost," posterior samples)\n\n", sep=""))
    res <- matrix(abc.out$unadj.values, ncol=np)
    mymin <- apply(res, 2, min)
    mymax <- apply(res, 2, max)
    mymean <- apply(res, 2, mean)
    mymode <- apply(res, 2, getmode, ...)
    quants <- apply(res, 2, quantile, probs = myprobs)
    sums <- rbind(mymin, quants[1,], quants[2,], mymean, mymode, quants[3,], mymax)
    dimnames(sums) <- list(c("Min.:", paste(c(myprobs[1])*100, "% Perc.:", sep=""),
                             "Median:", "Mean:", "Mode:",
                             paste(c(myprobs[3])*100, "% Perc.:", sep=""), "Max.:"),
                           parnames)
  }
  else{
    if(print){
      cat(paste("Data:\n abc.out$adj.values (",npost," posterior samples)\n", sep=""))
      cat(paste("Weights:\n abc.out$weights\n\n", sep=""))
    }
    res <- matrix(abc.out$adj.values, ncol=np)
    wt <- abc.out$weights
    mymin <- apply(res, 2, min)
    mymax <- apply(res, 2, max)
    mymean <- apply(res, 2, weighted.mean, w = wt)
    mymode <- apply(res, 2, getmode, wt/sum(wt), ...)
    quants <- apply(res, 2, function(x) rq(x~1, tau = myprobs, weights = wt)$coef)
    sums <- rbind(mymin, quants[1,], quants[2,], mymean, mymode, quants[3,], mymax)
    dimnames(sums) <- list(c("Min.:", paste("Weighted ", c(myprobs[1])*100, " % Perc.:", sep=""),
                             "Weighted Median:", "Weighted Mean:", "Weighted Mode:",
                             paste("Weighted ", c(myprobs[3])*100, " % Perc.:", sep=""), "Max.:"),
                           parnames)
  }
  class(sums) <- "table"
  if(print){
    if(length(digits) == 1) 
      print(round(sums, digits = digits), quote=FALSE)
    else
      print(apply(rbind(digits, sums), 2, function(a) round(a[-1], digits = a[1])), quote=FALSE)
    invisible(sums)
  }
  else sums
}

getmode <- function(x, weights = NULL, ...){

  ##  if(missing(bw) | missing(kernel) | missing(window) | missing(n)) warning("density.default() was used to calculate the posterior mode")
  d <- density(x, weights = weights)
  d$x[which(d$y == max(d$y))][1] 
}


hist.abc <- function(x, unadj = FALSE, true = NULL,
                     file = NULL, postscript = FALSE, onefile = TRUE, ask = !is.null(deviceIsInteractive()),
                     col.hist = "grey", col.true = "red", caption = NULL, ...){

  
  if (!inherits(x, "abc")) 
      stop("Use only with objects of class \"abc\".", call.=F)
  abc.out <- x
  np <- abc.out$numparam
  parnames <- abc.out$names[[1]]

  if(is.null(caption)) mycaption <- as.graphicsAnnot(parnames)
  else mycaption <- caption
  
  ## checks if true is given
  if(!is.null(true)){
      if(!is.vector(true)){
          stop("Supply true parameter value(s) as a vector.", call.=F)
      }
      if (length(true) != np){
          stop("Number of true values has to be the same as number of parameters in 'x'.", call.=F)
      }
      cond <- isTRUE(c(match(names(true), parnames), match(names(true), parnames)))
      if(cond) stop("Names do not match in 'x' and 'true'.", call.=F)
  }

  if(abc.out$method == "rejection") res <- abc.out$unadj.values
  else if (unadj){
    res <- abc.out$unadj.values
  }
  else res <- abc.out$adj.values

  ## Devices
  ## ##########
  save.devAskNewPage <- devAskNewPage()
  if(!is.null(file)){
    file <- substitute(file)
    if(!postscript) pdf(file = paste(file, "pdf", sep="."), onefile=onefile)
    if(postscript) postscript(file = paste(file, "ps", sep="."), onefile=onefile)
  }
  else{
    if (ask && prod(par("mfcol")) < np) {
      devAskNewPage(TRUE)
    }
  }

  myhist <- list()
  for(i in 1:np){
    myxlim <- range(res[,i], true[i])
    myhist[[i]] <- hist(res[,i], xlab = parnames[i], main = paste("Posterior histogram of ", mycaption[i], sep=""),
                        col = col.hist, xlim = myxlim, ...)
    myhist[[i]]$xname <- parnames[i]
    if(!is.null(true)){
      abline(v = true[i], lwd = 2, col = col.true)
    }
  }

  if(!is.null(file)){
    dev.off()
  }
  else devAskNewPage(save.devAskNewPage)
  
  names(myhist) <- parnames
  invisible(myhist)

} # end of hist.abc

3: #' Computes a confidence interval (and optional zero-correlation test) for the
4: #' Pearson correlation between two serially correlated series. It reduces the
5: #' nominal sample size N to an effective sample size N_eff based on each series'
6: #' lag-1 autocorrelation, then applies Fisher's z-transformation using N_eff.
7: #'
8: #' @param x,y       Numeric vectors of equal length (paired observations).
9: #' @param conf      Confidence level (default 0.95).
10: #'
11: #' @return A list with the correlation, effective sample size, CI bounds,
12: #'         and a t-test of H0: rho = 0 using N_eff.
13: #' @export
14: corr_ci_autocorr <- function(x, y, conf = 0.95) {
15: 
16:   # --- input handling: drop pairs with NA, check length ---------------------
17:   ok <- stats::complete.cases(x, y)
18:   x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]
19:   n <- length(x)
20:   if (n < 4L) stop("Need at least 4 complete paired observations.")
21: 
22:   # --- Pearson correlation --------------------------------------------------
23:   r <- stats::cor(x, y)
24: 
25:   # --- lag-1 autocorrelation of each series ---------------------------------
26:   rho_x <- stats::acf(x, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE, demean = TRUE)$acf[2]
27:   rho_y <- stats::acf(y, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE, demean = TRUE)$acf[2]
28: 
29:   # --- effective sample size for two AR(1) processes ------------------------
30:   #   N_eff = N * (1 - rho_x * rho_y) / (1 + rho_x * rho_y)
31:   prod_rho <- rho_x * rho_y
32:   n_eff <- n * (1 - prod_rho) / (1 + prod_rho)
33:   # Guard against pathological values; N_eff must exceed 3 for the SE below.
34:   n_eff <- min(n_eff, n)            # cap at nominal N (negative prod_rho case)
35:   if (n_eff <= 3) {
36:     warning("Effective sample size <= 3; interval is unreliable.")
37:     return(list(
38:       r          = r,
39:       conf       = conf,
40:       ci_lower   = NA_real_,
41:       ci_upper   = NA_real_,
42:       n          = n,

79: #'
80: #' Simulates `n` observations where `y = a*x1 + b*x2 + e`, with `x1` and `x2`
81: #' drawn independently (so no multicollinearity), then returns the estimated
82: #' coefficient of `x1` from a regression of `y` on `x1` alone.
83: #'
84: #' @param n Number of observations to simulate.
85: #' @param a True coefficient of `x1`.
86: #' @param b True coefficient of `x2`.
87: #'
88: #' @return The estimated coefficient of `x1` from `lm(y ~ x1)`.
89: #' @export
90: #'
91: #' @examples
92: #' hist(replicate(1000, lm_sim(100, -10, 10)))
93: lm_sim <- function(n, a, b) {
94: 
95:   x1 <- sample(1:100, size = n, replace = TRUE)
96:   x2 <- sample(1:100, size = n, replace = TRUE)
97: 
98:   e <- stats::rnorm(n)
99: 
100:   y <- a * x1 + b * x2 + e
101: 
102:   stats::coefficients(stats::lm(y ~ x1))[2]
103: }

106: #' Simulation to test how multi-collinearity affects estimates
107: #'
108: #' Simulates bivariate normal predictors `X1` and `X2` with covariance matrix
109: #' `covmat`, generates `Y = b0 + b1*X1 + b2*X2 + epsilon`, then fits three
110: #' regressions: the joint model (`Y ~ X2 + X1`) and each single-predictor
111: #' model. Returns the coefficient estimates from all three models stacked
112: #' together.
113: #'
114: #' @param n Number of observations to simulate.
115: #' @param mu1 Mean of `X1`.
116: #' @param mu2 Mean of `X2`.
117: #' @param b0 Intercept of the true model.
118: #' @param b1 True coefficient of `X1`.
119: #' @param b2 True coefficient of `X2`.
120: #' @param covmat 2x2 covariance matrix of `X1` and `X2`.
121: #'
122: #' @return A data frame with columns `term`, `value`, and `type` (`"joint"`
123: #'   for the joint model, `"single"` for the single-predictor models).
124: #' @export
125: #'
126: #' @examples
127: #' multicol_sim(
128: #'   n = 100, mu1 = 0, mu2 = 0, b0 = 1, b1 = 2, b2 = 3,
129: #'   covmat = matrix(c(1, 0.9, 0.9, 1), nrow = 2)
130: #' )
131: multicol_sim <- function(n, mu1, mu2, b0, b1, b2, covmat) {
132: 
133:   # Generate n random samples from a bivariate normal with covariance covmat
134:   L <- chol(covmat)
135:   z <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n * 2), nrow = n, ncol = 2)
136:   bivariate_data <- sweep(z %*% L, 2, c(mu1, mu2), "+")
137: 
138:   # Convert to a data frame for easier use
139:   df <- as.data.frame(bivariate_data)
140:   colnames(df) <- c("X1", "X2")
141: 
142:   # make linear model
143:   epsilon <- stats::rnorm(n)
144:   df$Y <- b0 + b1 * df$X1 + b2 * df$X2 + epsilon
145: 
146:   # Stack coefficient estimates from the joint model and each single-predictor
147:   # model into one data frame
148:   coef_table <- function(formula, type) {
149:     coefs <- stats::coefficients(stats::lm(formula, data = df))
150:     data.frame(term = names(coefs), value = unname(coefs), type = type)
151:   }
152: 
153:   rbind(
154:     coef_table(Y ~ X2 + X1, "joint"),
155:     coef_table(Y ~ X1, "single"),
156:     coef_table(Y ~ X2, "single")
157:   )
158: }

```r
#' Approximate Bayesian computation predictions on validation data
#'
#' Evaluates an ABC model similar to cross-validation: uses the training
#' simulations to predict the outcome of each validation simulation, and
#' repeats this for all validation data points. For every validation point,
#' `abc::abc()` is fit on the training simulations and summary statistics of
#' the posterior are recorded (95% credible interval bounds, mean, median,
#' and mode).
#'
#' @param train_sample  Data frame of training simulations (outcomes and
#'   summary statistics).
#' @param val_sample    Data frame of validation simulations.
#' @param outcomes      Character vector naming the outcome column(s) in both
#'   samples.
#' @param summary_stats Character vector naming the summary statistic
#'   column(s) in both samples.
#' @param tol           Acceptance tolerance passed to `abc::abc()`.
#' @param method        ABC method passed to `abc::abc()` (`"rejection"`,
#'   `"loclinear"`, `"neuralnet"`, or `"ridge"`).
#' @param verbose       If TRUE, print a progress message for each validation
#'   example.
#'
#' @return A data frame with one row per validation simulation and columns
#'   `truth`, `lwr_cred_int`, `pred_mean`, `pred_median`, `pred_mode`, and
#'   `upr_cred_int`.
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \donttest{
#' set.seed(1)
#' sims <- data.frame(Ne = 2^seq(4, 10, length.out = 500))
#' sims$mean_freq_change <- 0.001 / sqrt(sims$Ne) * exp(stats::rnorm(500, 0, 0.5))
#' train <- sims[1:400, ]
#' val <- sims[401:500, ]
#' train_abc(train, val, outcomes = "Ne", summary_stats = "mean_freq_change",
#'           tol = 0.1, method = "rejection")
#' }
train_abc <- function(train_sample, val_sample, outcomes, summary_stats, tol, method, verbose = FALSE) {
  if (!requireNamespace("abc", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("The abc package is required for train_abc().")
  }

  # vectors to store results
  lwr_results <- c()
  median_results <- c()
  mean_results <- c()
  mode_results <- c()
  upr_results <- c()

  # subset frames to relevant metrics
  train_outcomes <- train_sample[, outcomes]
  train_stats <- train_sample[, summary_stats]
  val_stats <- val_sample[, summary_stats]

  # loop over validation data
  for (i in 1:nrow(val_stats)) {
    if (verbose) message("Validation example: ", i)

    # get one validation simulation
    val_target <- val_stats[i, ]

    # run abc on validation sim
    invisible(utils::capture.output(
      result <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
        abc::abc(val_target, train_outcomes, train_stats, tol, method)
      )),
      type = "output"
    ))
    result_summary <- summary(result, print = FALSE)
    cred_int <- round(c(result_summary[[2]], result_summary[[6]]))
    median_est <- round(result_summary[[3]])
    mean_est <- round(result_summary[[4]])
    mode_est <- round(result_summary[[5]])

    # save prediction
    lwr_results <- c(lwr_results, cred_int[1])
    median_results <- c(median_results, median_est)
    mean_results <- c(mean_results, mean_est)
    mode_results <- c(mode_results, mode_est)
    upr_results <- c(upr_results, cred_int[2])
  }

  return(
    data.frame(
      truth = val_sample[, outcomes],
      lwr_cred_int = lwr_results,
      pred_mean = mean_results,
      pred_median = median_results,
      pred_mode = mode_results,
      upr_cred_int = upr_results
    )
  )
}
```

Wait — one issue. `result_summary[[2]]` etc. — when print=FALSE, summary.abc returns `sums` (the matrix) invisibly. The matrix rows are: Min., 2.5% Perc., Median, Mean, Mode, 97.5% Perc., Max. So [[2]] is 2.5th percentile, [[3]] median, [[4]] mean, [[5]] mode, [[6]] 97.5th percentile. Indexing a matrix with [[ ]] goes column-major. With one parameter, one column, so [[2]] is row 2 = 2.5% percentile. That works.

But wait — when print = FALSE, the function does `else sums` — returns sums but NOT invisible? Let me check:

    else
      print(apply(rbind(digits, sums), 2, function(a) round(a[-1], digits = a[1])), quote=FALSE)

```

Also `cred_int <- round(c(result_summary[[2]], result_summary[[6]]))` — result_summary is a matrix with dimnames. c() of two 1-length extractions gives a numeric vector of 2. Good.

```r
test_that("train_abc recovers outcomes on simulated validation data", {
  skip_if_not_installed("abc")

  set.seed(42)
  n_sim <- 300
  sims <- data.frame(Ne = 2^seq(4, 10, length.out = n_sim))
  # summary statistic correlated with the outcome
  sims$mean_freq_change <- 0.1 / sqrt(sims$Ne) * exp(stats::rnorm(n_sim, 0, 0.3))

  train <- sims[1:250, ]
  val <- sims[251:300, ]

  preds <- train_abc(
    train_sample = train,
    val_sample = val,
    outcomes = "Ne",
    summary_stats = "mean_freq_change",
    tol = 0.2,
    method = "rejection"
  )

  expect_s3_class(preds, "data.frame")
  expect_identical(names(preds), c("truth", "lwr_cred_int", "pred_mean", "pred_median", "pred_mode", "upr_cred_int"))
  expect_identical(preds$truth, val$Ne)
  expect_equal(nrow(preds), nrow(val))
  # credible intervals bracket the point predictions
  expect_true(all(preds$lwr_cred_int <= preds$pred_mean))
  expect_true(all(preds$pred_mean <= preds$upr_cred_int))
})
```

```json
{
  "filePath": "/home/miles/miles-rventures/R/statistics.R",
  "oldString": "  rbind(\n    coef_table(Y ~ X2 + X1, \"joint\"),\n    coef_table(Y ~ X1, \"single\"),\n    coef_table(Y ~ X2, \"single\")\n  )\n}",
  "newString": "  rbind(\n    coef_table(Y ~ X2 + X1, \"joint\"),\n    coef_table(Y ~ X1, \"single\"),\n    coef_table(Y ~ X2, \"single\")\n  )\n}\n\n\n#' Approximate Bayesian computation cross-validation\n#'\n#' Evaluates an ABC model the way a neural network is validated: after\n#' \"training\" on a set of simulated parameter/summary-statistic pairs, each\n#' validation data point is predicted using the training data alone. Each\n#' validation simulation is used as the ABC target in turn, and the posterior\n#' is summarized by its credible interval, mean, median, and mode.\n#'\n#' Requires the `abc` package (installed separately; it is only suggested by\n#' this package).\n#'\n#' @param train_sample Data frame of training simulations; columns selected by\n#'   `outcomes` and `summary_stats`.\n#' @param val_sample Data frame of validation simulations with the same\n#'   columns.\n#' @param outcomes Character vector naming the outcome (parameter) column(s).\n#' @param summary_stats Character vector naming the summary statistic\n#'   column(s).\n#' @param tol ABC acceptance tolerance, passed to `abc::abc()`.\n#' @param method ABC method, passed to `abc::abc()` (`\"rejection\"`,\n#'   `\"loclinear\"`, `\"neuralnet\"`, or `\"ridge\"`).\n#' @param verbose If `TRUE`, emit a message for each validation example.\n#'\n#' @return A data frame with one row per validation simulation and columns\n#'   `truth`, `lwr_cred_int`, `pred_mean`, `pred_median`, `pred_mode`, and\n#'   `upr_cred_int`.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' \\donttest{\n#' sim_stats <- data.frame(\n#'   Ne = c(100, 200, 500, 1000),\n#'   S1 = c(1, 2, 3, 4)\n#' )\n#' train_abc(\n#'   train_sample = sim_stats, val_sample = sim_stats,\n#'   outcomes = \"Ne\", summary_stats = \"S1\",\n#'   tol = 0.5, method = \"rejection\"\n#' )\n#' }\ntrain_abc <- function(train_sample, val_sample, outcomes, summary_stats, tol, method, verbose = FALSE) {\n\n  if (!requireNamespace(\"abc\", quietly = TRUE)) {\n    stop(\"The abc package is required for train_abc(). Install it with install.packages('abc').\")\n  }\n\n  # vectors to store results\n  lwr_results <- c()\n  median_results <- c()\n  mean_results <- c()\n  mode_results <- c()\n  upr_results <- c()\n\n  # subset frames to relevant metrics\n  train_outcomes <- train_sample[, outcomes]\n  train_stats <- train_sample[, summary_stats]\n  val_stats <- val_sample[, summary_stats]\n\n  # loop over validation data\n  for (i in 1:nrow(val_stats)) {\n    if (verbose) message(\"Validation example: \", i)\n\n    # get one validation simulation\n    val_target <- val_stats[i, ]\n\n    # run abc on validation sim; abc() and summary.abc() write to stdout with\n    # cat()/print(), which suppressMessages()/suppressWarnings() cannot touch,\n    # so divert stdout with capture.output() and use print = FALSE\n    result <- invisible(utils::capture.output(\n      result <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(\n        abc::abc(val_target, train_outcomes, train_stats, tol, method)\n      )),\n      type = \"output\"\n    ))\n    result_summary <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(\n      summary(result, print = FALSE)\n    ))\n\n    cred_int <- round(c(result_summary[[2]], result_summary[[6]]))\n    median_est <- round(result_summary[[3]])\n    mean_est <- round(result_summary[[4]])\n    mode_est <- round(result_summary[[5]])\n\n    # save prediction\n    lwr_results <- c(lwr_results, cred_int[1])\n    median_results <- c(median_results, median_est)\n    mean_results <- c(mean_results, mean_est)\n    mode_results <- c(mode_results, mode_est)\n    upr_results <- c(upr_results, cred_int[2])\n  }\n\n  return(\n    data.frame(\n      truth = val_sample[, outcomes],\n      lwr_cred_int = lwr_results,\n      pred_mean = mean_results,\n      pred_median = median_results,\n      pred_mode = mode_results,\n      upr_cred_int = upr_results\n    )\n  )\n}"
}
```
