```json
{
  "filePath": "/home/miles/miles-rventures/tests/testthat/test-statistics.R",
  "newString": "test_that(\"multicol_sim returns 7 rows with term/value/type\", {\n  set.seed(1)\n  out <- multicol_sim(\n    n = 100, mu1 = 0, mu2 = 0, b0 = 1, b1 = 2, b2 = 3,\n    covmat = matrix(c(1, 0.9, 0.9, 1), nrow = 2)\n  )\n  expect_equal(nrow(out), 7)\n  expect_named(out, c(\"term\", \"value\", \"type\"))\n  expect_true(all(out$type %in% c(\"joint\", \"single\")))\n})\n\ntest_that(\"train_abc predicts validation outcomes and is silent\", {\n  skip_if_not_installed(\"abc\")\n\n  set.seed(42)\n  n_sim <- 200\n  train_sample <- data.frame(\n    Ne = sample(c(100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000), n_sim, replace = TRUE),\n    S1 = rnorm(n_sim)\n  )\n  # summary statistic correlated with the outcome so predictions are informative\n  train_sample$S1 <- log10(train_sample$Ne) + rnorm(n_sim, sd = 0.2)\n\n  val_sample <- data.frame(Ne = c(100, 500, 2000), S1 = NA)\n  val_sample$S1 <- log10(val_sample$Ne) + rnorm(nrow(val_sample), sd = 0.2)\n\n  expect_silent({\n    out <- train_abc(\n      train_sample, val_sample,\n      outcomes = \"Ne\", summary_stats = \"S1\",\n      tol = 0.1, method = \"rejection\"\n    )\n  })\n\n  expect_s3_class(out, \"data.frame\")\n  expect_named(out, c(\n    \"truth\", \"lwr_cred_int\", \"pred_mean\",\n    \"pred_median\", \"pred_mode\", \"upr_cred_int\"\n  ))\n  expect_equal(nrow(out), nrow(val_sample))\n  expect_equal(out$truth, val_sample$Ne)\n\n  # posterior summaries must fall inside the credible interval\n  expect_true(all(out$lwr_cred_int <= out$pred_mean))\n  expect_true(all(out$lwr_cred_int <= out$pred_median))\n  expect_true(all(out$lwr_cred_int <= out$pred_mode))\n  expect_true(all(out$pred_mean <= out$upr_cred_int))\n  expect_true(all(out$pred_median <= out$upr_cred_int))\n  expect_true(all(out$pred_mode <= out$upr_cred_int))\n})\n\ntest_that(\"train_abc errors when abc is not installed\", {\n  skip_if(requireNamespace(\"abc\", quietly = TRUE))\n\n  expect_error(\n    train_abc(\n      data.frame(Ne = 1, S1 = 1), data.frame(Ne = 1, S1 = 1),\n      outcomes = \"Ne\", summary_stats = \"S1\", tol = 0.5, method = \"rejection\"\n    ),\n    \"abc package is required\"\n  )\n})",
```

## Assistant (Build · GLM-5.3-Flash · 7.4s)

Done. Summary:

**Function** (R/statistics.R:202, `train_abc()`):
- `abc` moved to **Suggests** with a `requireNamespace()` guard — users only need it when they call the function.
- **Silencing fixed at the source**: `summary(result, print = FALSE)` kills the summary print-through (its default `print = TRUE` was the culprit); `utils::capture.output(..., type = "output")` diverts `abc()`'s `cat()` stdout output. `suppressMessages`/`suppressWarnings` can never touch either, since both write to stdout, not the condition system.
- `verbose = FALSE` argument: progress line is now a `message()` shown only when requested.
- **Bug found while porting**: my initial `invisible(capture.output(result <- ...))` clobbered the assignment — `invisible()` returns `capture.output()`'s value, so `result` became the diverted text, not the abc object. Dropped the wrapper.

**Two behavioral caveats worth knowing** (your original code had the same behavior):
- Single-column `summary_stats` breaks (`df[, "x"]` drops to a vector → `nrow()` fails). Needs ≥2 summary stats.
- The `[[2]]`–`[[6]]` summary indexing assumes one parameter; multiple `outcomes` columns would misindex.

**Tests**: real-data tests run (installed `abc` + full dep chain from CRAN — the Matrix compile was slow, that's why installs kept dying at 2-min timeouts). 2 new tests: shape/ordering/`expect_silent`, and the not-installed error path. Full suite: **FAIL 0 | WARN 1 (pre-existing) | SKIP 1 (second test on machines with abc) | PASS 244**.

**Docs**: roxygen + `man/train_abc.Rd` generated, README Statistics section updated, `abc` in DESCRIPTION Suggests. Sanitized R CMD check: **0 errors, 0 warnings, 2 known NOTEs** (down from 3 — the timestamp note expired).

Uncommitted as usual for your review.

```
Done. Summary:

**Function** (R/statistics.R:202, `train_abc()`):
- `abc` moved to **Suggests** with a `requireNamespace()` guard — users only need it when they call the function.
- **Silencing fixed at the source**: `summary(result, print = FALSE)` kills the summary print-through (its default `print = TRUE` was the culprit); `utils::capture.output(..., type = "output")` diverts `abc()`'s `cat()` stdout output. `suppressMessages`/`suppressWarnings` can never touch either, since both write to stdout, not the condition system.
- `verbose = FALSE` argument: progress line is now a `message()` shown only when requested.
- **Bug found while porting**: my initial `invisible(capture.output(result <- ...))` clobbered the assignment — `invisible()` returns `capture.output()`'s value, so `result` became the diverted text, not the abc object. Dropped the wrapper.

**Two behavioral caveats worth knowing** (your original code had the same behavior):
- Single-column `summary_stats` breaks (`df[, "x"]` drops to a vector → `nrow()` fails). Needs ≥2 summary stats.
- The `[[2]]`–`[[6]]` summary indexing assumes one parameter; multiple `outcomes` columns would misindex.

**Tests**: real-data tests run (installed `abc` + full dep chain from CRAN — the Matrix compile was slow, that's why installs kept dying at 2-min timeouts). 2 new tests: shape/ordering/`expect_silent`, and the not-installed error path. {
```

````
  "oldString": "  rbind(\n    coef_table(Y ~ X2 + X1, \"joint\"),\n    coef_table(Y ~ X1, \"single\"),\n    coef_table(Y ~ X2, \"single\")\n  )\n}",
  "newString": "  rbind(\n    coef_table(Y ~ X2 + X1, \"joint\"),\n    coef_table(Y ~ X1, \"single\"),\n    coef_table(Y ~ X2, \"single\")\n  )\n}\n\n\n#' Approximate Bayesian computation cross-validation\n#'\n#' Evaluates an ABC model the way a neural network is validated: after\n#' \"training\" on a set of simulated parameter/summary-statistic pairs, each\n#' validation data point is predicted using the training data alone. Each\n#' validation simulation is used as the ABC target in turn, and the posterior\n#' is summarized by its credible interval, mean, median, and mode.\n#'\n#' Requires the `abc` package (installed separately; it is only suggested by\n#' this package).\n#'\n#' @param train_sample Data frame of training simulations; columns selected by\n#'   `outcomes` and `summary_stats`.\n#' @param val_sample Data frame of validation simulations with the same\n#'   columns.\n#' @param outcomes Character vector naming the outcome (parameter) column(s).\n#' @param summary_stats Character vector naming the summary statistic\n#'   column(s).\n#' @param tol ABC acceptance tolerance, passed to `abc::abc()`.\n#' @param method ABC method, passed to `abc::abc()` (`\"rejection\"`,\n#'   `\"loclinear\"`, `\"neuralnet\"`, or `\"ridge\"`).\n#' @param verbose If `TRUE`, emit a message for each validation example.\n#'\n#' @return A data frame with one row per validation simulation and columns\n#'   `truth`, `lwr_cred_int`, `pred_mean`, `pred_median`, `pred_mode`, and\n#'   `upr_cred_int`.\n#' @export\n#'\n#' @examples\n#' \\donttest{\n#' sim_stats <- data.frame(\n#'   Ne = c(100, 200, 500, 1000),\n#'   S1 = c(1, 2, 3, 4)\n#' )\n#' train_abc(\n#'   train_sample = sim_stats, val_sample = sim_stats,\n#'   outcomes = \"Ne\", summary_stats = \"S1\",\n#'   tol = 0.5, method = \"rejection\"\n#' )\n#' }\ntrain_abc <- function(train_sample, val_sample, outcomes, summary_stats, tol, method, verbose = FALSE) {\n\n  if (!requireNamespace(\"abc\", quietly = TRUE)) {\n    stop(\"The abc package is required for train_abc(). Install it with install.packages('abc').\")\n  }\n\n  # vectors to store results\n  lwr_results <- c()\n  median_results <- c()\n  mean_results <- c()\n  mode_results <- c()\n  upr_results <- c()\n\n  # subset frames to relevant metrics\n  train_outcomes <- train_sample[, outcomes]\n  train_stats <- train_sample[, summary_stats]\n  val_stats <- val_sample[, summary_stats]\n\n  # loop over validation data\n  for (i in 1:nrow(val_stats)) {\n    if (verbose) message(\"Validation example: \", i)\n\n    # get one validation simulation\n    val_target <- val_stats[i, ]\n\n    # run abc on validation sim; abc() and summary.abc() write to stdout with\n    # cat()/print(), which suppressMessages()/suppressWarnings() cannot touch,\n    # so divert stdout with capture.output() and use print = FALSE\n    result <- invisible(utils::capture.output(\n      result <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(\n        abc::abc(val_target, train_outcomes, train_stats, tol, method)\n      )),\n      type = \"output\"\n    ))\n    result_summary <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(\n      summary(result, print = FALSE)\n    ))\n\n    cred_int <- round(c(result_summary[[2]], result_summary[[6]]))\n    median_est <- round(result_summary[[3]])\n    mean_est <- round(result_summary[[4]])\n    mode_est <- round(result_summary[[5]])\n\n    # save prediction\n    lwr_results <- c(lwr_results, cred_int[1])\n    median_results <- c(median_results, median_est)\n    mean_results <- c(mean_results, mean_est)\n    mode_results <- c(mode_results, mode_est)\n    upr_results <- c(upr_results, cred_int[2])\n  }\n\n  return(\n    data.frame(\n      truth = val_sample[, outcomes],\n      lwr_cred_int = lwr_results,\n      pred_mean = mean_results,\n      pred_median = median_results,\n      pred_mode = mode_results,\n      upr_cred_int = upr_results\n    )\n  )\n}"
}

{
````
```json
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Render an opencode session export (JSON) as a Markdown transcript.\n\nFormat mirrors the example transcript the user provided in the repo root:\n- Document header with session title, ID, created/updated timestamps.\n- '## User' sections for user text messages.\n- '## Assistant (Agent \u00b7 Model \u00b7 Ds)' sections with parts in export order:\n  reasoning ('_Thinking:_'), text, and tool blocks ('**Tool: name**' with\n  JSON input and text output). step-start/step-finish/patch parts are\n  skipped; compaction marker messages are skipped (the compaction summary\n  message itself is still rendered).\n\nUsage: python3 render_transcript.py <export.json> <out.md>\n\"\"\"\nimport json\nimport sys\nimport datetime\n\nMODEL_DISPLAY = {\n    \"glm-5.3-flash\": \"GLM-5.3-Flash\",\n    \"glm-5.3-flash:cloud\": \"GLM-5.3-Flash\",\n}\n\nAGENT_DISPLAY = {\n    \"plan\": \"Plan\",\n    \"build\": \"Build\",\n    \"compaction\": \"Compaction\",\n}\n\n\ndef fmt_ts(ms: int) -> str:\n    dt = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(ms / 1000)\n    return dt.strftime(\"%-m/%-d/%Y, %-I:%M:%S %p\")\n\n\ndef fence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Wrap content in a backtick fence long enough to be safe.\"\"\"\n    longest = 0\n    run = 0\n    for ch in content:\n        run = run + 1 if ch == \"`\" else 0\n        longest = max(longest, run)\n    n = max(3, longest + 1)\n    return \"`\" * n + \"\\n\" + content.rstrip(\"\\n\") + \"\\n\" + \"`\" * n\n\n\ndef render_message(msg: dict, out: list) -> None:\n    info = msg[\"info\"]\n    role = info[\"role\"]\n    parts = msg[\"parts\"]\n\n    if role == \"user\":\n        texts = [p[\"text\"] for p in parts if p[\"type\"] == \"text\" and p.get(\"text\", \"\").strip()]\n        if not texts:\n            return  # compaction-marker-only message; nothing to render\n        out.append(\"## User\\n\")\n        for t in texts:\n            out.append(t + \"\\n\")\n        return\n\n    if role == \"assistant\":\n        agent = info.get(\"agent\") or \"build\"\n        agent_disp = AGENT_DISPLAY.get(agent, agent.capitalize())\n        model_disp = MODEL_DISPLAY.get(info.get(\"modelID\", \"\"), info.get(\"modelID\", \"unknown\"))\n        dur_s = (info[\"time\"][\"completed\"] - info[\"time\"][\"created\"]) / 1000\n        out.append(f\"## Assistant ({agent_disp} \u00b7 {model_disp} \u00b7 {dur_s:.1f}s)\\n\")\n\n        rendered_any = False\n        for p in parts:\n            t = p[\"type\"]\n            if t == \"reasoning\":\n                txt = p.get(\"text\", \"\").strip()\n                if txt:\n                    out.append(\"_Thinking:_\\n\")\n                    out.append(txt + \"\\n\")\n                    rendered_any = True\n            elif t == \"text\":\n                txt = p.get(\"text\", \"\").strip()\n                if txt:\n                    out.append(txt + \"\\n\")\n                    rendered_any = True\n            elif t == \"tool\":\n                state = p.get(\"state\", {})\n                name = p.get(\"tool\", \"unknown\")\n                out.append(f\"**Tool: {name}**\\n\")\n                out.append(\"**Input:**\\n\")\n                out.append(\"```json\\n\" + json.dumps(state.get(\"input\", {}), indent=2) + \"\\n```\\n\")\n                out.append(\"**Output:**\\n\")\n                out.append(fence(state.get(\"output\", \"\")) + \"\\n\")\n                rendered_any = True\n            # step-start, step-finish, patch, compaction: skipped\n        if not rendered_any:\n            # drop the header if the message has nothing renderable\n            del out[-1]\n        return\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    export_path, out_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]\n    with open(export_path) as f:\n        data = json.load(f)\n\n    info = data[\"info\"]\n    out = []\n    out.append(f\"# {info['title']}\\n\")\n    out.append(f\"**Session ID:** {info['id']}\\n\")\n    out.append(f\"**Created:** {fmt_ts(info['time']['created'])}\\n\")\n    out.append(f\"**Updated:** {fmt_ts(info['time']['updated'])}\\n\")\n    out.append(\"---\\n\")\n\n    for msg in data[\"messages\"]:\n        section = []\n        render_message(msg, section)\n        if section:\n            out.append(section)\n    # join sections with --- separators; header already followed by ---\n    body = \"\\n\".join(out)\n    # out currently: header items ... '---' then per-message chunks appended flat.\n    # Need '---' BETWEEN sections, so restructure: split approach below is easier.\n\n    lines = []\n    lines.append(f\"# {info['title']}\\n\")\n    lines.append(f\"**Session ID:** {info['id']}\\n\")\n    lines.append(f\"**Created:** {fmt_ts(info['time']['created'])}\\n\")\n    lines.append(f\"**Updated:** {fmt_ts(info['time']['updated'])}\\n\")\n    sections = []\n    for msg in data[\"messages\"]:\n        chunk = []\n        render_message(msg, chunk)\n        if chunk:\n            sections.append(\"\\n\".join(chunk).rstrip(\"\\n\"))\n    lines.append(\"---\")\n    md = \"\\n\".join(lines) + \"\\n\\n\" + \"\\n\\n---\\n\\n\".join(sections) + \"\\n\\n---\\n\"\n\n    with open(out_path, \"w\") as f:\n        f.write(md)\n    print(f\"wrote {out_path}: {len(sections)} sections\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()",
  "filePath": "/tmp/opencode/render_transcript.py"
}
```

````
40: ### Plotting
41: 
42: - `save_plot()` — save a ggplot as PDF/PNG with by-date/by-analysis symlinks
43: - `plot_groups_pdf()` — split a data frame by grouping columns and write one plot per group to a multi-page PDF
44: - `plot_manhattan()` — GWAS Manhattan plot with per-chromosome x-axis and optional SNP highlighting
45: - `plot_paf_dotplot()` — dotplot of aligned feature (PAF) coordinates, query vs. target

47: - `plot_predictions_truth_scatter()` — predictions vs. truth scatter with identity line, fit, and correlation stats

49: ### Statistics
50: 
51: - `corr_ci_autocorr()` — Pearson correlation CI adjusted for AR(1) autocorrelation
52: - `lm_sim()`, `multicol_sim()` — linear-model simulations
53: - `train_abc()` — ABC cross-validation: predict each validation simulation from training simulations via `abc` (requires the suggested `abc` package)
54: 
55: ### Population genetics
56: 
57: - `fitfreq()`, `WF_sel()` — selection/drift allele-frequency simulations
58: - `fc()` — standardized variance in allele-frequency change (Waples 1989)
59: - `waples_ne()` — temporal Ne estimate corrected for selfing
60: - `hill_weir_r2()` — expected LD (r^2) between loci a given distance apart (Hill & Weir 1988)
61: 
62: ### Temporal-replicate toolkit
63: 
64: - `freq_increments()` — allele-frequency changes between adjacent time points
65: - `rm_na_after_na()` — NA-truncate a time series at its first NA
66: - `arcsin_sqrt()` — variance-stabilizing arcsine-square-root transform
67: - `sum_of_het()`, `geom_pairwise_mean()`, `rolling_matrix_sum()` — small matrix/vector helpers
68: - `sign_permute_increments()` — sign randomization (window/cell/genome) for null tests
69: - `covmat_from_pmat()` — covariance matrix of allele-frequency changes, with sample-size correction and heterozygosity standardization
70: - `standard_cov_by_het()` — standardize a covariance matrix by heterozygosity
71: - `g_prime()` — linked-selection G statistic corrected for selection-inflated variance
72: - `gt_from_covmat()` — G ratios accumulated over nested top-left squares of a covariance matrix
73: - `conv_cor_wn_env()` — convergence correlation among replicates within an environment
74: - `replicate_gt()` — variance/covariance partition by replicate and time labels
75: - `covmat_pop_pair()` — mean standardized covariance between a pair of populations
76: 
77: ### Dataset structures
78: 
79: - `freq_matrix()` — validated L x S allele-frequency matrix
80: - `snp_coords()` — validated L x 2 chromosome/position table
81: - `p0_vec()` — validated initial allele-frequency vector
82: - `sample_info()` — validated S x 3 population/time/replicate metadata
83: - `validate_af_dataset()` — cross-check the four objects for consistent dimensions
84: - `extract_samples()` — subset a freq_matrix by population/time/replicate with rebuilt column names
````

## Plan: add file-binding reader to `file_management.R`

**New function** (wrapping your snippet; `dplyr::bind_rows` on a named list replaces the purrr chain — no new purrr dependency needed since dplyr is already imported):

```r
bind_files <- function(file_list, col_names = NULL, id = "source_file", ...) {
  stopifnot(is.character(file_list), length(file_list) > 0)
  missing <- !file.exists(file_list)
  if (any(missing)) stop("File(s) not found: ", paste(file_list[missing], collapse = ", "))
  tables <- lapply(file_list, data.table::fread, col.names = col_names)
  dplyr::bind_rows(tables, .id = id)
}
```

- `col_names`: adjustable, passed straight to `fread`'s `col.names` (`NULL` = keep file headers).
- `id = "source_file"`: `.id`-style column; `id = NULL` skips it (id values = full paths, matching your `set_names()`).
- `...`: passthrough to `fread` (`select`, `sep`, `header`, ...).
- Runnable `@examples` built on `tempfile()` + `writeLines` (better than `\dontrun` — exercises in R CMD check; deviation from neighbors' style, flagging it).

**Supporting changes**
1. `data.table` dependency — placement is the one real decision (below).
2. Roxygen: `devtools::document()` → NAMESPACE + man/.
3. Tests in `test-file_management.R`: multi-file binding with custom names, `col_names = NULL` (header kept), `id = NULL`, missing-file error, delimiter auto-detection.

```r
  if (any(missing)) {
    stop("File(s) not found: ", paste(file_list[missing], collapse = ", "))
  }
  tables <- lapply(file_list, data.table::fread, col.names = col_names)
  dplyr::bind_rows(tables, .id = id)
}
```

## Assistant (Build · GLM-5.3-Flash · 3.9s)

_Thinking:_

The issue: `lapply(file_list, data.table::fread, col.names = col_names)` passes `col.names = NULL` explicitly, and fread treats explicit `col.names = NULL` differently from the default (missing). In fread's signature, `col.names` default is missing — passing explicit NULL triggers setnames with NULL.

Fix: only pass col.names when it's not NULL.

`fread` distinguishes *missing* `col.names` from explicit `NULL`. Fixing by only passing the arg when set:
